John 1. **COME, SEE**, (Dear reader, before you judge it, come first and see it for yourself—according to the Weimar Glossary.) Therefore, dear reader, do not be quick to believe what the evil-academic <note>original: *Caco-Academischen*, a play on "cacophony" and "academic," implying scholars who produce harsh or discordant ideas</note> artists and faculty members say; come, read it yourself, though without preconceived delusions. etc.

> *Tertullian, from the book On the Veiling of Virgins, p. 490.*
> *Truth cannot be dictated to by any person: not by the passage of time, nor by the patronage of individuals, nor by the privileges of regions.* <note>original Latin: *Veritati nemo potest præscribere, non spacium temporum, non Patrocinia personarum, non privilegia regionum.*</note>

It does not make Jacob Böhme a heretic simply because such a teaching has not been heard for a long time, nor because many distinguished, perverse-learned men—**learned in word and letter, but not truly so named and not spiritually taught** <note>original Latin: *verb: & liter: non nomin. & spiritualiter docti*</note>—are against it. Nor does it matter that many provinces give, take, and use privileges, power, law, and freedom to slander Böhme, ordering people to accept common, sworn confession-formulas and statutes (as the Mark of the Beast, **Revelation 13:17**). Or that whoever does not carry this "mark" has no privilege to come to the fairs <note>referring to the great trade fairs of the era</note>, to buy or to sell, but must instead be cast under the ban as a dreamer, fool, and visionary <note>original: *Schwermer*, a derogatory term for religious enthusiasts or fanatics</note>—along with his books—by the superlative "Teacher-Fools" <note>original: *Docen-Thoren*, a pun on *Dozenten* (lecturers) and *Thoren* (fools)</note> at the "Un-versity" <note>original: *Unverstät*, a pun on *Universität* (university) and *Unverstand* (lack of understanding)</note>. These people reveal themselves as heresy-makers who seek to maintain their worldly kingdom not with truth, but with bans and force. As enemies of Christ and followers of the Antichrist-like Pharisees, they reveal themselves to all the world against their own will and show whose spirit’s children they truly are.

### II.

This book is such a noble jewel as the sun has never shone upon since the time of the Apostles; this book is the foundation of all treasures of wisdom, as much as can be expressed in written letters, founded upon the cornerstone which the builders rejected <note>A reference to Psalm 118:22 and Acts 4:11, identifying the book's foundation with Christ.</note>, and it is full of divine and natural wonders which the merciful, kind **GOD** shares with us mortals out of His unfeigned love, from His eternal and primordial treasures. Within it, the entire divine **Magic**, **Angelic Kabbalah**, and **Natural Philosophy** <note>original: *Magia, Englische Cabala, und Natürliche Philosophia*.</note> are revealed quite nakedly to the children [of wisdom], so that my heart rejoices whenever I think of this book. 

But know this: whoever desires to understand this book must not be a **sensual**, **rational**, or **animal man** <note>original: *Sensualis, Rationalis, Animalis Homo* — referring to those who live only by physical senses, worldly logic, or basic biological instincts.</note>, but rather a **mental**, **spiritual man**, **illuminated by the light of the light of divine grace** <note>original: *Mentalis, Spiritualis, ex Lumine Luminis Gratiæ Divinæ Illuminatus Homo*.</note>.

1. For know this, that the spirit of man reaches into **God**.
2. The mind of man reaches into the angels. For the spirit is divine, the mind is angelic <note>original: *Englisch* — meaning pertaining to angels.</note>.
3. The body of man reaches into the earth, for it is earth, ashes, and dust.

Know this as well: the pure body is a **salt**, the pure soul a **fire**, the pure spirit a **light** <note>original: *Saltz, Seel, Geist* — Böhme uses these as alchemical and spiritual categories to describe the makeup of a perfected human being.</note>. ### To the Reader.

<image-desc>A decorative woodcut initial 'L' decorated with scrolling foliage and floral motifs.</image-desc>
Dear reader / I consider the lampoon / to be worth no answer / because nothing but pure untruth and blasphemies are found therein / however, I have wished to make an answer for the sake of those / who do not understand it and have not read my little book / nor know my person / who look only upon the status / of the Chief Pastor <note>original: "Primarius."</note> / and think he slanders me out of Christian zeal / and does such a thing for God's sake because of his office / just as the greater crowd is thus led astray / so that they give him their approval / and think he does right / and that everything he screams from the pulpit must be true / because he uses God’s name therein / and cloaks it so / that one cannot see his furious heart / and also appeals to his office / so that the simple-minded believe it / who know nothing of the matter / how maliciously he persecutes me / and acts entirely against his office / and never wished to hear me regarding these things. And he judges that / which he himself does not understand; so I have made an answer / so that many might perhaps become seeing / and turn away from slandering against God’s gift / and I testify herewith before God / that I have answered from no other intention than purely for the sake of love for my neighbor / and I admonish the Chief Pastor to change his mind for the better : For he does not have a lion before him / but a little sheep of Christ / or he shall see / whom he has pricked / so that the sheep in the spirit of Christ does not become a lion to him / and the sheep judges the wolf / and I mean this heartily and faithfully.

You also despise / that I am a layman <note>original: "Lay," meaning someone without formal university training in theology</note> / and have not come from the university <term>high school: "hohen Schul," referring to the academic institutions where clergy were trained</term> / with my knowledge / and you scoff at my gift / which I have nonetheless received from GOD / as a noble gift / which is also dearer to me / than the whole world / and you also shame my trade <note>Böhme was a shoemaker</note> with your scoffing / and call it along with my gift a stench.

The spirit which now gladdens you / so that you may vent your courage with blasphemy and slandering / against me / that might yet well become a hellish fire for you / and eat into your conscience / where will you remain then?

# Defense.

You force tears and earnest prayers from me against your blasphemies / by accusing me entirely with untruths / see to it / that my tears do not become glowing coals upon your head : I have prayed much for you to God / that God would enlighten you / and give you the truth to recognize : But you become ever more wicked with blasphemy / I shall be innocent regarding you / whether God's wrath would touch you.

Dear Mr. Lead Pastor <note>original: "Primarius," the title of the head clergyman of the city</note>, why do you despise me / because I am a layman / and have divine and natural knowledge. Do you think / that the Holy Spirit is bound to your schools? for Christ our Beloved spoke / my Father will give the Holy Spirit / to those who ask him for it. Also / Ask / and you shall receive / knock / and it shall be opened unto you / etc.

<margin>+</margin>
I have received my gift through earnest asking and knocking / and have tasted such a thing / that I would not give it for all the world's honor and goods / nor can I ever deny it / why do you attribute the gift of God to the Devil? Look back into the world / what simple people God has often used for his work.

Who were Abel, Seth, Enoch, and Noah? Who were the patriarchs? Shepherds / who were also not Doctors <note>referring to academic degrees in theology</note>. Who was Moses? a shepherd! Who was David? A shepherd! Who were the prophets / especially Elisha <note>original: "Eliseus"</note> and Habakkuk <note>original: "Habacuc"</note>? Simple and pious people! Who dealt with agricultural work. Who was Mary / the mother of Christ: A poor / pious / orphaned maiden? Who was Christ's foster-father in his childhood? a carpenter! Who were Christ's Apostles? altogether poor / simple craftsmen / like fishermen and the like; Why did Christ not also reject them / because they had not studied? Did he also scoff at them / because they were craftsmen / as you do?

What was the beginning of the Christians' nobility? Humility and the fear of God!
Where does your great boast in the Scripture with <term>art</term> <note>original: "Kunst," meaning human learning, academic skill, or formal theology</note> lie? show it to me! St. Paul was a scribe / but when he became a Christian / he first had to become a fool in his art and wisdom / so that Divine wisdom might find a place within him. Why then do you boast of your art / if you otherwise call yourself a Christian / do you not know / that in Christ we are all only One / that is / Christ in us all / so us Christ teaches and loves / why then do you curse us / and help to kill Christ in us : Confess it.

It does not have a bad appearance / as if the evil spirit were in you / who cannot endure Christ / who does not stand with you alone / which you cannot deny / because you say / there is a blasphemy in every line / and forbid people to read it / upon [pain of] eternal punishment.

Dear Mr. Lead Pastor, open your heart! and read the little book correctly / you will find something else therein / you have never yet read it / I see that from the title of your <note>original: "Pasqvils," a satirical or slanderous public attack</note>, for you state the title incorrectly / and have never yet seen the little book of <term>True Resignation</term> <note>original: "Gelassenheit," Böhme’s term for yielding the individual will to God</note>, of the *Imitation of Christ* / therein / you put the *Aurora* <note>original: "Morgenröthe," Böhme's first work, meaning "The Day-Spring" or "Morning Glow"</note> for the first book / of which you know little and nothing / and *The Way to Christ* for the other little book / [the treatise] of Repentance you put for the third / and it is the first in the printed [volumes] / and you have never yet seen the last.

-> A 3 <-

You draw tears and earnest prayers out of me against your blasphemy, in that you accuse me entirely with untruths; see to it that my tears do not become glowing coals upon your head. Why then do you boast of your art, if you call yourself a Christian? Do you not know that in Christ we are all but one? That is, Christ in us all. If Christ teaches and loves us, why then do you curse us and help to kill Christ within us? It is a **stench** <note>meaning a shameful or foul-smelling act in a spiritual sense</note>.

->**The Lampoon**<-
<note>original: "Pasqvil." Böhme uses this term to label the specific insulting accusations made by the Pastor.</note>

26. You also say that a great punishment hangs over those places where such blasphemy is devised, spread, and believed without being punished—where people may boldly and unhindered devise, write, and believe whatever they wish.

->**The Response**<-

27. Yes, dear Mr. Head Pastor, I also believe that a great punishment hangs over those places where people blaspheme God's gift and attribute it to the Devil. Furthermore, a great punishment certainly hangs over the **earthly man** <note>In Böhme’s theology, the "earthly man" is the ego-driven self that must be overcome.</note> when such an earnestness of repentance is practiced; for he must be killed daily and made a fool before the world if he is to walk the Divine way.

28. You see well how I am punished by you in such ways; and not only by you, but you also set the entire city upon my neck with slandering, so that they believe you and punish me. But it is **Christ’s mark of distinction** <note>original: "Christi Wahlzeichen," referring to the suffering or "cross" that identifies a true follower of Christ.</note>.

29. But that you prescribe a "model of faith" for the people, so that each should not believe according to his Divine gift as the Spirit of God reveals it in their souls—that requires another sort of lampoon; this one does not satisfy them.

30. But that you threaten them with punishment—that I believe you well enough. Had you the power, they would have to go into the fire, or all be driven out of the country.

31. That you also say the way to repentance is an "invented teaching"—the New Testament does not say so! For when Christ began His Gospel with John the Baptist, He said: "**Repent!**" And my little book says that too!

32. Mr. Head Pastor, the **natural man** <term>Natural man: A person living only by their physical senses and reason, without spiritual enlightenment.</term> perceives nothing of this way. You have no need to punish him; he goes well enough into the Devil's ways without that, until Christ enlightens him in repentance. ->Response.<-
<note>original: "Responsio."</note>

34. I also hold it to be true and firmly believe that GOD will let no Devil take His honor—which He has revealed in Jesus Christ, through the victories over death and hell, within us poor humans—much less will He let a **Head Pastor** <note>original: "Primar."</note>, **Doctor**, **Peter**, **Shoemaker**, **Tailor**, **Tanner**, or **Weaver** take it. Rather, those among these who shall perform repentance and turn to Him, to them He will grant His honor. I also believe that He Himself will rescue His children from all evil and make them blessed.

->The Lampoon.<-
<note>original: "Pasqvil."</note>

35. The poison of **Arius** <note>Arius (c. 250–336 AD) was a priest who taught that Jesus Christ was not eternal but was created by God the Father. This was declared a heresy at the Council of Nicaea.</note>, who denied the eternity of the Son of God, was not so wicked nor so harmful as the **Shoemaker’s poison**, which takes away the eternal Father’s eternity and, in a blasphemous manner, teaches a **Quaternity** <term>Quaternity: A "four-foldness" of God. Orthodox Christianity teaches a Trinity (Father, Son, Holy Spirit). Richter accuses Böhme of adding a fourth element, which would be a radical heresy.</term> or four-fold nature.

36. The people of the East were punished with **Mohammedan darkness** <note>A common 17th-century European view that the rise of Islam in the Byzantine Empire was a divine punishment for the Arian heresy.</note> because of the Arian heresy; what terrible punishment then must we expect if we do not, with due earnestness, hunt this poison away from our Fatherland and root it out entirely?

->Response.<-

37. Mr. Head Pastor, to these things I say a loud **no**: You could never prove in all eternity that I take from GOD the Father His eternity, much less that I teach a plurality of gods. For a long time, you have baselessy fabricated things against me and applied a foreign understanding to my writings. You have said from the pulpit that I had written that the Son of GOD was made of **mercury**; you shall prove that, or it shall eternally remain an untruth—and such an untruth is truly shameful.

38. I profess one single GOD, who is the eternal, beginningless, single good Being, who dwells within Himself outside of all nature and creation, and requires no place nor space, nor is He subject to any measurement, much less any conception of nature or creature. And I profess that this One is **Triune in Person**, equal in omnipotence and power: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.

39. And I profess that this Triune Being simultaneously fills all things, and was and still is the ground and beginning of all things.

40. Furthermore, I believe and profess that the eternal power (as the Divine Breathing or Speaking) flowed out and became visible; in which out-flown Word the inner heaven and the visible world stand, along with all created beings: that GOD made all things through His Word.

41. Mr. Head Pastor, when I wrote of **Nitre** <note>original: "Salniter." In Böhme's alchemy, this refers to a divine "saltpeter" or the explosive, creative power of God's nature.</note> and **Mercury** in the *Aurora* <note>Böhme’s first book, "Aurora, or the Morning Redness."</note>, I did not mean the pure, clear GOD Himself; I meant His out-flown, substantial Word, acting as a shadow of the inner ground. Through this, the Word led itself into a natural working and thereby made itself material. Thus, I point to the **Three Principles** in nature (as a spiritual **Mercury, Sulfur, and Salt**) <term>The Three Principles: Also known as the *Tria Prima*. In Böhme's thought, these are not just chemicals but spiritual forces that govern the manifestation of all matter.</term>, what their ground and origin might be, since all of nature and all creatures stand within them.

42. I have written of **three births**: an eternal, beginningless Divine birth; a Holy birth, in which light and darkness are understood as God’s love and wrath; and a beginning and temporal birth (such as the visible world). I understand the Nitre and Mercury to be in this third birth—that is, in the created beings.

100. Christ taught the people the Divine Commandments; this man, however, teaches ecstasy with great earnestness.

->The Response<-

101. O Lord <term>Head Pastor: <note>original: "Primarius"</note> The chief minister of a city's churches; here, Gregor Richter.</term>! Where does it stand in my book that I teach people external <term>ecstasy: <note>original: "Verzuckung"</note> A state of trance or being "carried away." Richter uses this to accuse Böhme of being a fanatic/mystic whose teachings lead people away from sober obedience to the law.</term>? Show me that! Or will it not be so: I teach them the **anointing of Jesus Christ**, with his tender humanity, in a spiritual manner within us, according to the inward ground of faith, of which Christ says: *He who eats my flesh and drinks my blood remains in me, and I in him; and he who does not eat the flesh of the Son of Man has no life in him* (John 6).

102. For that is the temple of the Holy Spirit, as Saint Paul says, where Christ’s flesh and blood remain in us. Likewise, it is the new **rebirth**, wherein the Holy Spirit searches the depths of the Godhead; it is the outpoured Word of the outpoured Divine Love, which marries and falls in love with our souls, just as the entire New Testament teaches, and as it is written, etc.

103. Test whether Christ has taken shape in you; if Christ is to gain a shape in us, he must not be absent. If we are to be branches on the vine of Christ, we must not cling to another: for *no one can serve two masters*, says Christ. Likewise: *My Father will give the Holy Spirit to all who ask Him for it*; likewise: *When the same comes, he will glorify you.*

104. It is not an external ecstasy, but an **internal illumination**, from which the soul—when it tastes this **Oil of Joy**—enters into such great joy, as is mentioned in my booklet about the noble **Sophia** (as the essential Love of <note>Jacob Böhme uses his initials "J.B." here in the third person.</note> J. B.).

105. Lord Head Pastor, I understand full well that you do not know this noble **Sophia**; it is not a good sign that you deny her and call her a <term>fanatic: <note>original: "Enthusiastinn"</note> Literally a "female enthusiast." In the 17th century, "Enthusiasm" was a derogatory term for someone claiming direct inspiration from God outside of church hierarchy.</term>. I know her well and I love her, for she is my soul's dear bride; if I did not know her, I would certainly not have suffered so much from you and others for the sake of her love.

106. Christ spoke: *He who does not enter through me to the sheep, as into the sheepfold of Christ, but climbs in elsewhere, is a thief and a murderer, and only a hireling, and has only come to rob the sheep of their wool.* But you say: "He who does not enter through the **universities** <note>original: "hohen Schulen"</note> is a thief and a murderer," and you mock the Door of Christ—which is the anointing of the Holy Spirit—and you want to have things your way, and you bind God’s gift to human <term>academic skill: <note>original: "Kunst"</note> Refers to human learning, artifice, or technical theological training.</term>.

109. 110. Lord Head Pastor, I say to you in love—mark my words well—I have received it from GOD so that I know it; the New Testament also teaches me this throughout. I have clearly indicated to you in my booklet that no human being can know or understand the **Noble Sophia** <note>Divine Wisdom, often personified in Böhme's work as the bride of the soul.</note> in the receptive love of JESUS CHRIST, unless it be given to them by GOD.

111. If that should happen—which I truly wish—then I would speak further with you about it. For now, you are not yet worthy of it, because you despise it.

112. For this reason, your teaching is also so cold, because you do not have this power within you. You do not yet have the right hammer for the bells; you certainly have the Word, but the power is not in you, where you ought to be working alongside the literal Word. Therefore Christ said: *the sheep do not hear his voice*.

113. This power, which I mean, is the door to the sheep. O Lord Head Pastor, in your slandering you often use Satan’s hammer under Christ’s purple mantle; your heart is full of gall and bitterness. Yet, it is time.

115. Lord <term>Head Pastor: <note>original: "Primarius." Refers to Gregor Richter, Böhme's chief antagonist.</note></term>, I do not lead people away from the preached and written Word; you do me wrong in that regard. I say, however, that they should bring the temple of Jesus Christ to the preached or written Word as a repentant, hungry soul, which hears Christ, the living Word, teaching within itself. As David says: *I will hear what the Lord says in me* <note>A mystical reading of Psalm 85:8, where Böhme emphasizes the "in me" as an internal revelation.</note>; and Christ spoke: *He who is of God hears God’s word* <note>John 8:47</note>; and to the Pharisees He said: *Therefore you do not hear, because you are not of God*; likewise: *You are not my sheep.*

116. Thus, my meaning is that a person must have divine ears, as a repentant soul, if he wish to hear Christ’s voice, whether it be in preaching, in reading, or in speaking. For this is what Christ has taught us, and I believe Him more than all <term>academic art: <note>original: "Kunst." Böhme often uses this to refer to scholarly or "man-made" theological systems as opposed to divine revelation.</note></term>. For <term>historical faith: <note>original: "historische Glaube." Böhme's term for intellectual belief in the Bible as a record of facts without experiencing its spiritual power personally.</note></term>—with its knowing, <term>speculating: <note>original: "kügeln." Literally "to roll little balls," a Böhme-ism for over-intellectualizing or ruminating on dogma without spirit.</note></term> and comforting, yet without power and an earnest will—is dead and only a husk; it does not achieve the state of childhood <note>referring to being a "child of God."</note>; there must be earnestness.

117. Lord Head Pastor, it is not enough that we go to churches and to the <term>Sacrament: <note>The Lord's Supper or Eucharist.</note></term>, and sit there for an hour, putting on a show of piety and hearing the sermon, while <term>stubble and wheat: <note>A metaphor for false and true teachings mixed together.</note></term> are sown together because you sometimes engage in such slandering. No, going to church is of no use at all unless one then actually hears God’s Word in their soul within the church. For the Prophet says: *With their mouth they draw near to me, but their heart is far from me.*

118. Not all who go to church and say LORD, LORD, shall enter the kingdom of heaven, but those who do the will of my Father in heaven, says Christ; not only to believe historically, but to act with power.

119. Therefore, hypocrisy and mere "teachability" do not count, for right faith is not just an imagined concept, but it is power, spirit, and life; it is a fire of the divine Word that burns and shines around itself, which works with God. Right faith is the <term>throne of God: <note>original: "Stuhl Gottes."</note></term> upon which God sits and speaks.

120. Faith is not a mere "historical breath" where one only comforts oneself and plays the hypocrite to the <term>evil beast: <note>Böhme’s term for the unrefined, selfish human nature or the "old Adam."</note></term> full of false desires. No, it is the living, actual power of God; its burning fire is the fire-flaming love of GOD, which breaks forth and does the work.

124. This makes Satan anxious, for he will no longer be tolerated under Christ’s purple mantle. Böhme’s term for the ego or the selfish, fallen nature of man.</note></term>.

->Response.<- <note>original: "Responsio."</note>

129. Christ said: *Come to me, all you who are weary and burdened* <note>A reference to Matthew 11:28.</note>; He made no distinction between the rich and the poor who come to Him. However, it vexes the <term>Head Pastor: <note>original: "Herrn Primarium," referring to Gregor Richter.</note></term> that someone is called to visit God-fearing wealthy people. By this, he perhaps means that he is losing something, believing that he alone is entitled to associate with the rich for his own personal gain, and that wealth belongs to him alone. Otherwise, he would honor the Shoemaker for his great wealth in this world <note>Böhme is likely speaking ironically here, contrasting Richter's obsession with material status against spiritual value.</note>, for the Shoemaker is not proud, as one can plainly see.

->Lampoon.<- <note>original: "Pasqvil."</note>

130. Christ lived His life in sobriety, but the Shoemaker is commonly accustomed to being drunk and full.

->Response.<-

131. Christ was indeed sober; but that which the Head Pastor attributes to the Shoemaker, he is himself. One is accustomed to picking up the Head Pastor from under the table in a state of drunkenness and leading him home. One could likely find the Head Pastor drunk more often in a single week than the Shoemaker in three years.

132. The Head Pastor took this article of accusation from his own conduct. Saint Paul says in Romans 5 <note>The text cites Romans 5, but the quote actually comes from Romans 2:1-3.</note>: *Therefore, O man, you have no excuse, whoever you are who judges. For in passing judgment on another, you condemn yourself, because you, the judge, practice the very same things. For we know that the judgment of God is right upon those who do such things.*

->Lampoon.<-

133. Christ certainly refrained from excessive laughter, but the Shoemaker laughs at everything he says.

->Response.<-

134. One does not find that Christ laughed; rather, He only rejoiced in spirit. However, that the Head Pastor attributes laughter and "fantasizing" to the Shoemaker, saying that he laughs at every word, may well be a great and public falsehood that cannot be proven. No truthful man could say such a thing. Furthermore, nature gives one person a greater tendency to laugh and be friendly than another, while another is made <term>Saturnine: <note>original: "Saturnischen." In the "four humors" theory of the time, a Saturnine person was influenced by the planet Saturn, making them naturally gloomy, sour, or melancholic.</note></term> and sour; the Head Pastor cannot change this, and he would do well to keep silent about it. If one were to describe him and his own foolish antics—the kind he often displays while carousing at the tavern—one would have to present strange <term>monsters: <note>original: "monstra." Here referring to grotesque or unnatural behaviors.</note></term>.

# Jacob Böhme

135. I am nearly struck with wonder that the <term>Head Pastor <note>original: "Herr Primarius," referring to Gregor Richter.</note></term> is not ashamed—given that he is an old man from whom one should expect wisdom—to write such public untruths and foolish antics, and to have an honest man printed as a figure of mockery. These are indeed worse than the <term>pranks of Eulenspiegel <note>A reference to Till Eulenspiegel, a famous German trickster figure known for his practical jokes and vulgarity.</note></term>; this satirical lampoon is almost identical to the filthy antics of <term>Marcolphus <note>A reference to the medieval dialogue "Solomon and Marcolf," in which the character Marcolf is known for his coarse, scatological wit.</note></term>, for he likewise always carries dung in his mouth, just as this lampoon does.

136. It reflects poorly on a teacher of Christ, who should forbid such things in others while practicing them himself. The pastoral office is poorly served by this; one should certainly not entrust their soul to such antics, or they would be deceived. This spirit stands on sand and is dizzy; one should judge him by such foolish behavior.

137. One knows the bird by its feathers. Christ said: *What is within comes out; what the heart is full of, the mouth overflows with.* <note>A paraphrase of Matthew 12:34.</note> Likewise: *How can you, being evil, speak good things? Can one gather grapes from thistles, or figs from thorns? A good man brings forth good things out of the treasure of his good heart, and an evil man brings forth evil out of the treasure of his evil heart.* <note>A paraphrase of Matthew 12:33-35 and Luke 6:43-45.</note>

138. I now give this to the reader to consider: what kind of "good treasure" the Head Pastor must have in his heart when he brings forth such strange things? Certainly, many more peculiar things must be hidden within him, which he is perhaps a little ashamed to release because he is the <term>High Priest <note>Böhme refers to Richter’s status as the highest-ranking clergyman in Görlitz.</note></term>. But if one goes to him and provokes him with even a single word, one sometimes hears Satan laughing out of him with blasphemies.

144. Christ did not desire royal honor; but the Shoemaker, if only he could, would gladly be King and God.

145. Christ came to earth poor, that He might have mercy on us and make us rich in heaven and equal to His dear angels. He also desires, in Christ, according to his inward ground of faith, to be <term>deified <note>original: "vergöttet." And even if the whole world were full of such lampoons, I would still keep my kingdom in Christ and tread the lampoons underfoot, and would not even spare my outward life for it. I know of a better life which Christ my Lord will give me.

149. Christ’s title was the Father's will; his honor was in God, and he introduced that same honor into our humanity and exalted our humanity to the right hand of the power of God. He has given that same honor to his Christians, so that they too might be in him at the right hand of the power of God and rule over sin, death, the devil, and the world. The Shoemaker also claims this high title and desires the highest royal title: the victory of our Lord Jesus Christ, as a knight over death and hell. He desires such a high title so that he may be victorious in the struggle against death and hell, and so that he might intend to overcome the whole world in Christ and be a king in Christ—and to rule over all the hostile lampoons and slanders of the <term>Head Pastor <note>original: "Primarius," referring to Gregor Richter.</note></term>. Otherwise, he desires no worldly titles, for the kingdom of Christians is not of this world; for Christ says, *I have called you out of this world, that you may be where I am.*

150. But the Lord Head Pastor certainly desires titles, for he has set his title of the High Priestly office and his own person in his lampoon with coarse letters, so that one should see the judge who has power over Christ’s children. Furthermore, if someone were to come too close to him and, out of terror, forget to <term>remove his hat <note>In the 17th century, removing one's hat was a mandatory sign of submission to social superiors. Böhme is accusing the Pastor of being more concerned with social ego than spiritual humility.</note></term>, he might very well receive a strange title, if he did not receive actual blows.

How then should the Lord Primarius not also fail to recognize the Shoemaker’s titles, since he knows he is a layman and does not recognize the name of Christ within him?

157. Christ gave the thirsty the Water of Life to drink; but the Shoemaker gulps down brandy—or the Water of Death—every morning.

->Response.<- <note>original: "Responsio." Latin for reply.</note>

158. Christ still offers his children the water of eternal life today, and drenches them with his blood of love. He also gives my thirsty soul that same water to drink; for this I thank him eternally, that he has made me alive and seeing through this water. I drink that same water, and it is a water for and against death—unlike the perverse way the Lord Primarius speaks of it.

159. But as for his claim that I run to brandy every morning, that is not true at all. I neither can nor wish to drink brandy, and I have had a long-standing enmity with brandy, so much so that I do not even like to smell it; it is repulsive to me. I am surprised that the Lord Primarius, as a High Priest <note>A sarcastic or pointed reference to Richter's ecclesiastical authority.</note>, errs so greatly; it truly suits him poorly. If a common man did that, people would say: "He is a liar." I hardly know what I should give as an answer to such untruth.

160. I firmly believe that this untruth was composed by the Satanic spirit of error. Lord Primarius, I advise you: drive that spirit away from you; it stains you immensely with such untruth. But if you wish to be right, then present an honest man to me—whether he be in the city or outside the city, or whoever he may be—who can say with truth that he sees me with brandy every morning. I appeal to the whole city and the Council Cellar <note>original: "Raths-Keller." The tavern or wine cellar typically located in the basement of the Town Hall, used for official city business and social gatherings.</note> to see if there is anyone who can say such a thing.

161. Lord Primarius, it is a great shame to you that you allow such untruth to be printed for the disgrace of others. With you, one might find large flasks and glasses of brandy; and just as you err and fail in this, so you fail in all articles of the <term>lampoon <note>original: "Pasqvills." A public written attack.</note></term>; not one is true according to your opinion.

# Defense Speech

->Response<- <note>original: "Responsio." Latin for reply.</note>

**163.** Christ turned water into good wine, and he himself is the good wine for thirsty souls, which my soul loves to drink. But as for the Lord Primarius <note>Gregor Richter, the head pastor of Görlitz.</note> saying that I enjoy guzzling foreign wine and brandy, he is only judging me by himself, thinking that others behave as he does. Oh no! We poor people do not have the money to pay for such things! We must make do with a drink of beer; but for the Lord Primarius, one must surely provide foreign wines, even if other people must settle for far less.

**164.** It is the Spanish wine that causes the Lord Primarius to lose himself at times. One can also see by the "wine-blood" <note>Referring to a flushed or ruddy complexion common in heavy drinkers.</note> in his face that he drinks much stronger wine than I do, for I have no such marks as he has. He drinks more foreign wine in a week than I drink in an entire year.

**165.** But I understand well enough "where the hare’s leg is broken" <note>A German idiom meaning "where the trouble lies" or "the root of the problem."</note>; he knows that by Divine Providence I have often been led to great lords and members of the nobility. So he thinks that when we come together, we sit and guzzle ourselves full, as he is accustomed to doing with his own company. But no! The nobles and powerful men who are served by drunkenness do not ask for me; only God-fearing, pious hearts who are earnest about their salvation seek me out.

**166.** This is nothing but envy from the Lord Primarius. He thinks he is losing something, but he need not fear that; these people who desire my company certainly do not desire his. There is a great difference between flattering someone and telling them the truth to their face. Whether the Lord Primarius believes it or not, it is not my habit to flatter the rich for the sake of gifts and presents, as he imagines.

**167.** I firmly believe that such rumors—offering old copper tins as if they were new measures <note>A metaphor for passing off worthless gossip as valuable news.</note>—were brought to him, and the good Lord believed it as if it were the Gospel, and wrote it down with great earnestness, becoming so enraged by it that he condemned the poor shoemaker without a hearing. But it will look very strange when the truth is sought and his answer is compared against the lampoon.

**168.** Dear Lord Primarius, it is truly a grave thing for a man such as you to so violate the truth. The city of Görlitz knows well that for a long time I have not entered any man's house unless out of necessity. The taverns and wine-cellars are left in peace by me, for you have treated me in such a way that I do not care to go anywhere. If I were to go into taverns and drink, how many hundreds of your "filths" <note>original: "Koden." This refers to the crude or offensive behavior/influence the pastor has allegedly spread among the common people.</note> would I encounter—those things you have poured into the common man, which are all your "fruits" that will follow you? You may well rejoice in them.

->Lampoon<- <note>original: "Pasqvil."</note>

**169.** Now that you recognize him by these traits—as one knows a lion by its claws—would you still want to read his books? Rather, avoid them as you would "devil's dung" and cruel error. Hold yourself simply to the Word of God and guard yourself against the Shoemaker's writings, whether you are a nobleman (or a doctor, tailor, man or woman) <note>original: "Adel (oder Doctor, Sartor, Vir sive Mulier)." Translating the Latin: Sartor (tailor), Vir (man), Mulier (woman).</note>. Lord Christ, restrain Satan’s tools, and do not let your Word be darkened. Yes! Yes, yes, yes—oh, let it be so, Amen!

<meta>This page continues Jacob Böhme’s defense against the libelous pamphlet (lampoon) written by the head pastor Gregor Richter. On the previous page, Böhme addressed Richter's accusations of drunkenness, contrasting Richter’s lifestyle with his own humble circumstances.</meta>

Jacob Böhme’s Response <note>original: "Responsio." Latin for reply.</note>.

**170.** It is well worth noting in these words why this lampoon <note>original: "Pasqvill," a published libel or satirical attack.</note> was written: namely, that he intends to destroy and completely root out me and my writings through such defamatory insults. The Devil is afraid that my writings are opening up his smoke-hole <note>A metaphor for exposing the devil's hiding places or foul vents.</note>; therefore, he paints me in such a color that no one shall read them, lest they might otherwise repent, which would cause a great loss to his kingdom.

**171.** But this Devil is far too coarse; he walks too exposed, so that people might notice him and learn to recognize him, for his claws are seen all too clearly in his envy and blasphemy—showing that he is an altogether poisonous spirit. It is now a completely different time; people no longer believe everything a person says right away. They also want to have proof. Why does he not provide proof from the printed booklets, instead of simply forbidding the congregation from reading them? Such defamatory slanders are no proof; one could just as well call them filth.

**172.** He speaks of the **Lion's Claws**, by which the **Shoemaker** <note>Böhme’s actual trade, which his critics used as a derogatory title to imply he was uneducated.</note> shall be recognized. Now, it is certainly true that the Lion's Claws will now be seen upon him <note>Referring to Richter, the attacker.</note>, and how the Lion has attacked and scratched the Shoemaker with contempt and insults; but the blood of JESUS Christ has resisted the Lion until now, otherwise the Lion would have torn the Shoemaker to pieces long ago.

**173.** But as for his saying that the Shoemaker's teaching is filth, he is thereby calling Christ’s mind and Spirit "filth." And regarding his warning that one should "beware of the Shoemaker's students," I say this: I know of no "students," but only of fellow Christians, where one soul refreshes another. I have no new teaching, but only the old one, which is to find in the Bible and in the realm of nature.

**174.** But that he calls his slanders "God’s Word"—saying that one should only hear from him and should blaspheme just as he does—I leave that to a Christian heart to consider, and to judge what kind of spirit he is of.

->**Response** <note>original: "Responsio."</note><-

**176.** Mr. Head Pastor <note>original: "Primarius."</note>, keep this travel-money <note>original: "Zehpfenning," a small sum given to a traveler or a "viaticum" for the dying; Böhme uses it sarcastically regarding Richter's "ascent" to heaven.</note> for yourself, for your own journey to heaven; I desire nothing from you. Your frivolous blasphemy will surely follow you as travel-money. Do not let yourself be so eager: *Let him who stands take heed lest he fall*; though you persecute me now and intend to banish me, who knows who will likewise persecute you in a short time.

**177.** The **Signature** <note>A central concept in Böhme’s philosophy; he believed the inner nature of all things is "signed" on their exterior.</note> is already at hand; it is only right that you should do to others what might later happen to you. You must indeed fill up your measure; and if you do not repent, the evil spirits might one day sing such a little grave-dirge to you, telling you to go far away from God’s countenance. For what you do to me now, you do to Christ in his members; that is what He will also do to you, unless you turn back and repent.

->**Lampoon** <note>original: "Pasqvil," referring to the satirical attack written by Richter.</note><-

**178.** You are like Oedipus (he means the **Sphinx** <note>original: "Sphingem." Richter appears to confuse the Greek myth of the Sphinx with the biblical story of Korah, whom the earth swallowed.</note>) whom the earth swallowed up; oh, beware that the same does not happen to you. This shadow greatly harmed the people who stood by him. But believe me, your shadow harms many of them most severely.

->**Response**<-

**179.** The **shadow of St. Peter** <note>A reference to Acts 5:15, where Peter's shadow healed the sick; Böhme flips the image to say his own presence only "harms" the wicked.</note> also greatly harmed the Devil; thus my shadow harms only the Devil and the **Antichrist**. (Perhaps you mean that my shadow might harm your earthly life, because I profess the **Imitation of Christ**; if the people were to accept such teaching, they would demand that you also live as the Apostles of Christ and follow their example—and that does not taste good to you. That is why you say my shadow harms some—namely the **false clergy**—most cruelly. That may well be true; it might turn out that way.)

**180.** However, I know very many spiritual priests whom it will not harm, but rather benefit greatly—those who take their office seriously. But who can account for Time, which brings all things to light?

**181.** If the Mr. Head Pastor were so faithful in his warning, he would stop his blaspheming from the pulpit and summon me to him privately to show me my error. If I found that he had any truth against me, and he showed me a better way, oh, how dearly I would love him and faithfully thank him for it! But he only rejoices that he has something he can use to blaspheme.

<summary>Böhme warns Richter that his insults will serve as his own "travel-money" to the afterlife and argues that Richter only fears Böhme's influence because it exposes the clergy's failure to live like the Apostles.</summary>

<meta>This page continues Jacob Böhme’s defense against the attacks of Gregor Richter, the Head Pastor of Görlitz. # Jacob Böhme

**182.** After his first blasphemy and persecution, I bowed down for six years and wrote not a single word. Why did he not stop his blaspheming? Who did anything to him? But he could not stop. Why? Because God had made him a **driving-hammer** <note>original: "Treibe-Hammer," a tool used to shape metal; Böhme suggests Richter’s attacks were the very thing that forced his spiritual work to be forged and completed.</note>, so that he was forced to drive the work forward.

**183.** His blasphemy has been my strength and growth; through his persecution, my **pearl** <note>Böhme often uses the "pearl" to represent the divine spark, wisdom, or the "new man" within the soul.</note> has grown. He pressed it out and even published it himself; therefore, I wish him God’s mercy, so that he might also enjoy it, since God has used him as my tool.

**184.** I would act much more humbly toward him if he converted than he has acted toward me. He must not think that I shy away from his face. I have a good conscience, and I wish him one as well.

**185.** To judge without a hearing is valid in no court of law. I do not submit myself to his judgment in such a manner, for my heart is not satisfied with his verdict. I am innocent of all the accusations; everything he has spoken against me from the pulpit is entirely against my meaning, and there is not a single true word in it. He has only twisted all my words with a foreign understanding.

**186.** Therefore, because I can currently have no other judge who is willing to understand my gift, I appeal from him and his **judgment** <term>Judicio <note>Latin: "Judicio," meaning a legal judgment or formal opinion.</note></term> to the court of my Savior JESUS Christ, until I am properly heard; then I will give an account of my affairs.

### Lampoon <note>original: "Pasqvil." This is the section where Böhme quotes Richter’s insults.</note>

**187.** Until now, you have followed **Cerinthus** <note>Cerinthus was an early Gnostic teacher and contemporary of the Apostle John, often cited by church authorities as a dangerous heretic.</note>, in that you have invented and "cooked up" strange things and cry out terrible matters. This Cerinthus, while he was bathing, insulted the LORD JESUS Christ and raged violently against God with his chatter. But the house collapsed and crushed him; and so the teacher perished along with his students.

### Response <note>original: "Responsio."</note>

**188.** Whether Cerinthus was against Christ, I leave that in its place; I am with Christ and confess Jesus Christ as my Lord and God, and I have submitted myself to him in obedience to live according to his commandments and will. But as for the **Head Pastor** <note>original: "Primarius."</note> saying that I have followed Cerinthus, that would certainly require proof, or else it will not be true.

**189.** But as for what he says regarding my "strange things," I say in truth that I have written nothing strange. I have only written what **nature** and **man** are. Because this seems "strange" to the Head Pastor, the fault lies only in the fact that he does not understand such things.

<meta>catchword: 190. What</meta>

<summary>Jacob Böhme defends his period of silence and interprets Pastor Richter's persecution as a divine tool that helped his spiritual development, while appealing his case to Christ's judgment. He specifically rebuts Richter's attempt to brand him a heretic by comparing him to the ancient Gnostic Cerinthus.</summary>
<keywords>Jacob Böhme, Gregor Richter, persecution, pearl, Cerinthus, heresy, divine judgment, nature of man, spiritual defense</keywords>

# Defense.

**190.** What can I do then, if he is blind to it? I have written nothing for him, but only for those to whom God gives understanding. Let him remain a High Priest <note>original: "Hoherpriester"; Böhme uses this title sarcastically to compare Richter to the legalistic religious authorities of the Bible.</note> and not become a philosopher or a student of nature, and then we are settled. He must not force the old sects upon me; I have seen none of their writings; it is nothing but his own malice.

->Lampoon.<- <note>original: "Pasqvil," a short, satirical poem or lampoon used for public mockery.</note>

**191.** Your filth, O Shoemaker, has greatly defiled our city.

->Response.<- <note>original: "Responsio."</note>

**192.** Mr. Head Pastor <term>Primarius <note>Latin: "Primarius," the lead minister or superintendent of a city's churches.</note></term>, you have so sprayed [the people] with the filth of blasphemy because of the Shoemaker, that many a person stinks of blasphemy. That is the filth that harms their souls—that they believe the blasphemy, take it into their hearts, and blaspheme God’s gift.

->Lampoon.<-

**193.** Oh, if only all those who read your writings would disappear along with you.

->Response.<-

**194.** What a Christian wish that is, coming from a High Priest! One would hardly find such a thing even with Caiaphas <note>Caiaphas was the Jewish High Priest who presided over the trial of Jesus; Böhme implies Richter is acting with the same persecutory spirit.</note>, and it surely would not be found anywhere in the Bible. It will soon come to pass that his "good wish" becomes true: that the sheep will be separated from the goats, so that the wicked have room in hell, since they can tolerate no one around them on earth.

->Lampoon.<-

**195.** Yes, you have even infected Silesia <note>A historical region now mostly in Poland, where Böhme’s ideas found a receptive audience among the nobility.</note> with your teaching, where you will be received by many—as I know for certain—people who, as they are much more distinguished in nobility than others, so they also lead others with their novelty. But you, his companions, guard and watch, so that these "distinguished writings" of this "distinguished man" do not perish.

->Response.<-

**196.** One finds now in Silesia many excellent, learned, God-fearing men who see much further than the Mr. Head Pastor, to whom their Christianity is a matter of true earnestness, and who walk in the imitation of Christ. They read many good little books which contain the true foundation. They did not first learn the imitation of Christ from me, but had it beforehand; yet they rejoice that God pours out such high knowledge even into simple people, which is indeed a miracle of God.

<summary>Böhme defends himself against Richter's public insults, arguing that it is the pastor's own blasphemy—not Böhme's writing—that defiles the city. He highlights the growing support for his work among the learned nobility of Silesia.</summary>

### Jacob Böhme’s Defense.
<meta>catchword: Send-</meta>

**197.** The Mr. Head Pastor <term>Primarius <note>Latin: "Primarius," refers to Gregor Richter, the lead minister of Görlitz.</note></term> attributes all of this to the Devil, just as the High Priests <note>Böhme refers to the religious authorities who condemned Jesus.</note> did to Christ; you follow in their "noble" footsteps. But the high-ranking nobility in Silesia <note>A region then in the Kingdom of Bohemia, now mostly in Poland, where Böhme had many supporters among the landed gentry.</note> take note of the times and see that **GOD** has something great in mind; but you are blind to it and are hardened. Therefore, the day of your punishment from **GOD** is coming and is near—know this.

->Lampoon.<- <note>original: "Pasqvil," a short, satirical or insulting public lampoon.</note>

**198.** Oh well, go then and never return, so that you might perish miserably; and take up a rope rather than a pen in your hand. <note>Richter is crudely suggesting that Böhme should hang himself rather than continue writing.</note>

->Response.<- <note>original: "Responsio."</note>

**199.** Christ said: *when they curse you, bless them, for then you are children of the most high God.* Because the Mr. Head Pastor wishes me a miserable death, his wish is from the Devil, for it runs entirely contrary to **GOD’s** commandment and will, as well as against all honest reason and integrity. By this, one shall know the tree by its fruits; and anyone may well consider from what spirit and disposition he persecutes me—that he does such things to please Satan and is no servant of Christ.

**200.** But because he curses me, I bless him through the blood and death of our Lord **JESUS** Christ, in the Name of **GOD** the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, Amen! And I wish for him that this blessing remains with him and gives birth to him as a child and heir of eternal life, so that he may become and eternally remain my brother in the life of our Lord **JESUS** Christ. Amen, Amen, Amen! And I conclude this with all my heart and will. Dated
->Görlitz, April 18, 1624.<-

<meta>This page transitions from the personal defense of Jacob Böhme against his primary antagonist, Pastor Gregor Richter, to a supporting letter written decades later by Ehrenfried Hegenitius. Hegenitius was a lawyer and a significant figure in the circle of Böhme’s followers in Görlitz, and this letter serves as a retrospective defense of Böhme’s legacy against the academic elite.</meta>

# Circular Letter
## From Mr. Ehrenfried Hegenitius,
### Dated Görlitz, February 21, 1669.

---

## GOD be with us in Grace.

My particularly favorable Lord and Friend. Your beloved letter from the past year reached me well: I should have answered sooner, had I not been prevented from doing so: I therefore ask you to hold me excused. Those who deny that a shoemaker <note>Referring to Jacob Böhme (1575–1624), the mystic and philosopher who worked as a master shoemaker in Görlitz.</note> is the author of the books in question give it to be understood that they do not believe that **GOD** can work in laymen who are without scripture and language—that is, in people unlearned in the letter; but rather that He wishes to speak His word and reveal His Spirit only through Latinists and those knowledgeable in other languages, and especially such men who have fetched their wit and subtle arts from the heights in Israel <note>A metaphorical reference to the elite theological faculties and university centers of the time.</note>. 

But they shall not take away **GOD’S** power: they are far too small for that. If they did not wish to be clever of themselves—that is, if they did not bring their understanding and judgment <term>judicium <note>Latin: "judicium," meaning the capacity for critical discernment or theological judgment.</note></term> into the Scriptures from the schools, or from a certain doctrine, norm, and form bounded by logical articles and often sworn to under oath; but instead brought it out of the Scriptures—as the testimony of **GOD**—into their school, no less than into other people's books, works, and wonders: then they might perhaps experience something else, and certainly believe what they cannot believe now due to their so deeply rooted school-madness <term>Schulwahn <note>A term used by Böhme’s followers to describe the rigid, institutionalized intellectualism of the university-trained clergy.</note></term>, in that they place such a delusion far above the gift of the Holy Spirit—indeed, in these current final times, they might even...

<summary>This letter by Ehrenfried Hegenitius defends the legitimacy of Jacob Böhme’s writings against critics who argued that an uneducated shoemaker could not produce such profound theological works. Hegenitius critiques the "school-madness" of university elites who believed divine revelation was restricted to those trained in Latin and formal logic.</summary>

<meta>This page continues Ehrenfried Hegenitius’s letter defending the late Jacob Böhme. Hegenitius recounts how, despite being too young to know Böhme personally during the height of the controversy with Pastor Gregor Richter, he later connected with Böhme’s inner circle and helped convince skeptical scholars of the shoemaker's genuine divine inspiration.</meta>

...matters, they would dare to deny these things, and yet they still wish to be called clergymen. It has not been so long since Jacob Böhme was still alive and his person was well enough known here. I, however, did not know him personally, because at the time when he first became famous for his book-writing, I was still somewhat young; and when, after several years, he took up writing again—which he had ceased by order of the authorities—and was branded a heretic from the pulpit by the Primary Pastor <note>Pastor Gregor Richter, Böhme’s chief antagonist in Görlitz.</note>, I was mostly absent. 

But in the year 1624, shortly after his death, I became acquainted with several of his most prominent friends and admirers, who had associated with him for a long time. It was Mr. Jonas Liebing, then a judge in Weißensee (four miles from Nuremberg), where I had stayed shortly before, who gave me the occasion for this; for he wrote to me twice and requested that I provide some certain report regarding Jacob Böhme for the sake of himself and Mr. Christian Becmann, Rector of the Gymnasium at Amberg. This was because they could not easily believe that an unlearned man <term>Idiot <note>Derived from the Greek 'idiōtēs,' this term in the 17th century referred to a layperson or a commoner without formal university training, particularly in Latin and theology.</note></term> should possess such a deep and extraordinary knowledge of God and nature. Becmann’s words in his letter, addressed to Liebing, are among others as follows:

> "Last winter a friend wrote to me: that in Görlitz there is a common man and otherwise unlearned <unclear>ignorant</unclear> <note>original Greek: ἀμαθῆ</note>, Jacob Böhme by name, who, imbued with a singular grace of the Spirit, both speaks various languages and, moreover, composes books full of much wisdom. From that time on, I did not cease to inquire anxiously whether it were so, etc. Finally, a few days ago, I came to Eger, and among other things there at a friend's house, I saw three manuscript books, and quite large ones at that, of this Böhme. What shall I say? As I read, I was astonished. Is it possible for a man from the masses, uneducated in school, to approach such profound mysteries and to write so elegantly! Indeed, the method itself and the exposition of hidden matters <note>original: "rerum abditarum"</note> makes me doubt the author. Böhme is said to be a layperson <term>idiota <note>A Latin term used here to describe someone who has not received a formal academic education.</note></term>; I cannot yet believe it; unless..."

->☛ ( 4 ) ☚<-

...mention was made: Thus he (Jacob Böhme) also knew everything—even if we spoke in Latin or French—that we had said. He also said we might speak in whatever language we wished, he would nonetheless understand it, and this by means of the **Nature-language** <term>Natur-Sprache: In Böhme’s thought, this is the primordial "sensual" language of Adam that expresses the inner essence of all created things.</term> which he knew, etc. Just as many other noble and distinguished people associated with him—often and even in secret, intimate friendship—so too did the noble Lord von Franckenberg <note>Abraham von Franckenberg (1593–1652) was Böhme’s most important biographer and a mystical writer who helped spread his ideas.</note> know him well and promoted the printing here in Görlitz <note>The town in Upper Lusatia where Böhme lived and worked as a shoemaker.</note> of his **booklet on Repentance, Resignation, and the Supersensual Life** in the year *1622* (under the title *The Way to Christ*). Regarding this von Franckenberg—in whose company I spent a long time in various places, and with whom I corresponded extensively through letters <note>original Latin: *per literas*</note> when away, so as not to forfeit his edifying conversation <note>original: *conversation*</note>—I could bring much testimony that it was J. B. himself, and not another under his name, through whom the wonders of God became manifest; for he [Franckenberg] had sufficiently observed them in his [Böhme’s] person. I will say nothing of those, not unknown to me, who through this man’s presence and piercing spiritual discourse underwent a remarkable and rapid transformation of their souls and a renewal of their lives: Thus, while previously they were entirely devoted to the vanity of this world and the lusts of the flesh, and behaved toward their subjects like nothing but ravening wolves, to everyone’s astonishment they afterwards became enemies of all decadence, treated their subjects like patient sheep, and wept over their former scandalous lives with constant repentance. From none of those who knew him have I ever heard, nor could I learn through others, that he was not accepted as the one who wrote the books which have since appeared under the name ***Teutonici*** <note>Latin: "The Teutonic [Philosopher]," the title by which Böhme became famous throughout Europe.</note> in High and Low German, as well as in English and partly in Latin. For if that were not the case, he would not have been sought out here by so many strangers, nor would he have been summoned to visit them; for certainly among these people were those who possessed the spirit of discernment, to whom he—on account of his high gifts—gave sufficient account, speech, and answer, providing no less than an abundant explanation of his books...

--- Page 56 ---
<meta>This page continues the defense of Jacob Böhme’s reputation and authorship. The previous page established through official records that Böhme was indeed the individual interrogated by church authorities in Dresden and Görlitz, countering claims that a simple shoemaker could not have written such profound works.</meta>

> "The Chief Pastor <note>original Latin: *Primarius*. This refers to Gregor Richter, the Superintendent of Görlitz and Böhme’s primary antagonist.</note> should have left the shoemaker in peace; he gained little honor from his actions. It would certainly have been much better: for the good man, the shoemaker—of whom I have never heard anything unseemly—would not have needed to write a formal defense <note>original Latin: *Apologiam*</note> against the pastor's libelous writings to save his honest name, thereby revealing the pastor's own shame. But the Chief Pastor, through the means of the world's slanderous tongues, ended up making Böhme known, and unintentionally promoted Böhme’s honor among impartial minds to his own disadvantage. In summary, during the lifetime of J.B., I believe there was no one here who did not consider him the true and sole author, or the true instrument, of the writings in question: it was only after his death that the ensuing new world, and those who did not know him—especially abroad—wanted to cast doubt on such high knowledge coming from a layman and a man of low standing."

A short biography <note>original German: *Lebens-Lauff*</note>, alongside the register of J.B.'s books, was composed in Latin <note>original Latin: *in Latein*</note> in the year 1637 by the aforementioned nobleman Abraham von Franckenberg <note>Franckenberg (1593–1652) was a Silesian nobleman and Böhme's most important early biographer and student.</note> and given to a good friend. This friend brought it to Amsterdam the following year, 1638, and translated it into High German to please a devotee <note>original German: *Liebhaber*, referring to a seeker or lover of divine truth</note>. Since that time, having been thus translated into German, it has been added to the published books. This was admittedly done without the prior knowledge of the author <note>original Latin: *Autoris*</note>, who, in such a complex case, would have brought the matter to light not only much more clearly (according to the nature of the German language), but also more extensively and with more detail; or else he might have completely concealed from the mocking world those divine mysteries which were found within Böhme’s person and made known to him above others. These works, which testify to this common man and "Friend of God"—namely his books, which are by now known here and there—are already sufficiently slandered by their despisers.

# The First Little Book
## On True Repentance.
### How a person must awaken themselves within their own will and mind,
and what their contemplation and earnest purpose should be when they wish to perform powerful repentance <note>original: *Busse*. In Böhme’s theology, this is not just a one-time apology, but a fundamental "turning around" of the soul’s direction.</note>, and with what kind of mind <note>original: *Gemühte*. A key term for Böhme, referring to the seat of the soul's emotions, desires, and will—the "inner disposition."</note> they should step before God when they wish to ask for and receive forgiveness of sins from God.

When a person wishes to proceed toward repentance and turn to God with their prayer, they should, before all prayer, examine their own mind: how it stands entirely turned away from God; how it has become unfaithful to God; how it is directed only toward this temporal, fragile, earthly life, and carries no true love toward God and its neighbor; and how it thus rages and storms entirely against God’s commandment, seeking only itself in temporal, transitory lusts of the flesh.

Secondly, they should consider how all of this is an enmity <note>original: *Feindschafft*. A state of active hostility or spiritual war against the divine order.</note> against God, which Satan—through his deceit—awakened in our first parents <note>A reference to Adam and Eve in the Garden of Eden.</note>; because of this abomination, we must die the death and suffer our bodies to decay.

Thirdly, they should consider the three cruel chains to which our soul is tightly bound during the time of this earthly life: the first of these is

### Warning to the Reader.

With good intentions, dear reader, I will not hide from you what has been earnestly shown to me here: if you are still comfortable in the vanity of the flesh, and are not in earnest purpose on the way to the **new rebirth** <term>original: "Wiedergeburt." The radical internal transformation of a person, turning from self-will to God's will.</term>, intending to become another person, then leave the above-written words in this prayer unspoken; otherwise, they will become a judgment of God within you. You shall not misuse the holy Name; be faithfully warned. These words belong to the needy soul; if she is truly in earnest, she will experience what they are.

### A Warning to the Reader.

Out of good intentions, dear reader, I will not hide from you what has been earnestly shown to me here: if you are still comfortable in the vanity of the flesh, and are not of an earnest purpose on the path to the new **rebirth** <term>original: "Wiedergeburt." Otherwise, they will become a judgment of God within you: you shall not misuse the holy name. Be faithfully warned; these words belong to the thirsty soul; if she is truly earnest, she will experience what they are.

# On True Repentance

O righteous God, you have indeed placed him in my stead; though he was innocent, and I am the one truly guilty <note>original: "Selbschuldige"—one who is personally responsible for their own debt or guilt.</note> for whom he suffered, why then should I despair in your wrath <note>original: "Grim"—this term implies a fierce, burning anger or fury, often depicted in this period as a physical force.</note>? Do with me as you will, only let me not deviate from his anguish. Have you not given his anguish to me as a gift and drowned your wrath in him? ## Instruction in Times of Temptation.

Kind Reader, it is no trifling matter; whoever has not experienced it and considers it a joke is yet unjudged. Even if this judgment were postponed until his final end—which is indeed dangerous—he must nevertheless pass through it. Oh, well is it for him who passes through it in early times, in the years of his youth, before the devil builds his castle of prey <note>original: "Raubschloß"—a metaphor for the state of sin where the devil holds the soul's faculties captive.</note> firmly within him. Such a person can afterwards become a worker in Christ’s vineyard and sow his seed in Christ’s little garden; he shall surely reap the fruits in due time. This judgment lasts for many a long time and many years if he does not earnestly put on Christ’s armor, especially when the judgment of temptation <term>Anfechtung: a state of spiritual trial, doubt, or assault from the devil where one feels abandoned by God.</term> must first exhort him to repentance. But for him who comes of his own earnest resolve and intends to depart from the godless way, it does not become so difficult, nor does it last long; although he must endure the knightly victory against the devil, he is nevertheless mightily assisted. It results in his greatest good, so that when afterwards the dawn <term>Morgenröte: literally "morning-redness"; in Böhme’s mysticism, it refers to the first light of divine illumination breaking into the darkness of the soul.</term> breaks in the soul, he may raise a great praise of God for the fact that the driver <note>original: "Treiber"—referring to the devil as a taskmaster or oppressor who goads the soul.</note> has been overcome.

Most gracious and deepest Love of God in Christ Jesus, give me your little pearl; <note>The "pearl" refers to the "Pearl of Great Price" from the parables, representing the inner kingdom of heaven or Divine Wisdom (Sophia).</note> press it into my soul, and take my soul into your arms.

O highest Love, you have appeared within me; stay within me and clasp me into yourself. Hold me within you so that I cannot depart from you. Fill my hunger with your love; feed my soul with your Heavenly Substance <term>Himlischen Wesen: in Böhme’s thought, this is the spiritual, "substantial" nourishment of the soul, contrasting with the temporary, material world.</term> and give it drink from your blood; give it drink from your little fountain.

Move it, I pray.

You have promised that your Father will give the Holy Spirit to those who ask him. So now I bring the hunger of my soul into your promise and take your word into my hunger. Increase my hunger within me for you; strengthen me, O sweet Love.

### To the Reader.

Dear reader, do not consider this to be some uncertain fiction <note>original: "Gedichte"; while it can mean "poem," in this context it refers to a made-up story or imaginative work</note>; it is the true foundation and contains within it the whole of Holy Scripture. He gives you the best that he has; may God grant the growth! A heavy judgment has been recognized upon the mocker of this work. Let him be warned.

# Preface

## To the God-loving Reader /

### On the true ground of the right Art of Prayer <note>original: "Beth-Kunst"; Böhme uses this term to suggest that prayer is a spiritual skill or "craft" that must be practiced and understood, rather than a rote ritual.</note> / What prayer is / and why GOD bids us pray.

<margin>1.</margin> <image-desc>Decorative woodcut initial C featuring ornate foliage and scrolling patterns.</image-desc>Dear Christian reader / to pray rightly is not merely a habit / as if one only needed to speak the words of the prayer : No / such word-speaking without heartfelt devotion <note>original: "Andacht"; refers to a state of being "collected" or focused in the presence of the Divine.</note> and Divine desire / is only an external thing / an external forming of words.

<margin>2.</margin> The mouth forms its words of prayer only with the external power of the stars <note>original: "Gestirnes"; in Böhme’s cosmology, the "stars" represent the natural, astral influences on the human body and mind, which are distinct from the deeper, eternal Spirit.</note> / and the elements / and creates only a form of the will / in which there is no actual power. For nothing pleases GOD except what He Himself works and does within a thing.

<margin>3.</margin> For GOD complains through the Prophet about such external mouth-prayers without power / where He says : With their lips they draw near to me / but their heart is far from me / Isaiah 29:13. <note>The source text cites "Es. 29. 14.", but this famous passage regarding lip-service is found in verse 13 of modern translations of Isaiah.</note> Likewise, Christ says : Not all / who say : LORD / LORD / shall enter into the kingdom of heaven / but those who do the will of my Father in heaven / Matthew 7:21.

# Instruction /
## How a person should prepare themselves for such order and exercise / for true prayer.

<image-desc>A large decorative drop-cap 'C' featuring ornamental floral and vine motifs.</image-desc>

**C**hristian dear reader: Right praying is also true earnestness <note>original: "Ernst"; a key term in Böhme’s thought, implying a deep, focused, and sincere spiritual intentionality.</note>, and must be in earnest, or it is invalid before **God**. For if we wish to pray correctly, we should think of nothing else than that we stand before **God’s** clear countenance, before the Holy Trinity, and before the choirs of his holy angels, and that **God** in our prayer tests our soul, spirit, and heart, and looks gantz intimately upon our will, to see whether it be directed entirely toward Him, and whether the will has surrendered itself completely to Him.

And if this is so, then He touches the will with the power of His Holy Spirit and shatters it <note>original: "zerschellet"; this suggests the breaking of the ego or the stubborn individual will so that it can be receptive to divine grace.</note>, so that it becomes truly desirous and hungry for grace, so that it begins earnestly to press out of itself and into **God’s** mercy.

For in its own strength the will is far too weak: But when the Divine power touches it, it is awakened so that it becomes fiery and truly desirous: In which desire **God** himself works; then the person speaks truly with **God**, and **God** speaks effectively <note>original: "würcklich"; here meaning "actively" or "with transformative power."</note> with the soul of the person.

# The Second Booklet /

Such speaking or working is nothing other than the poor soul eating of **God’s** mercy (which He has turned back toward us through the death of **Christ**) and refreshing itself with the balm of Divine Love in **Christ**, wherein it becomes strong against the assault <note>original: "Anfechtung"; a term used by Luther and Böhme for the spiritual struggle, doubt, and trial the soul feels under the devil’s influence.</note> of the devil.

For the Divine Hearing <note>This refers to God’s capacity to listen to us and our capacity to hear Him internally—a spiritual resonance.</note> is the power of grace which He has introduced back into humanity in the name **JESUS**, and has there opened again a gate for us to His hearing, through which we can hear **God** actually speaking within us, as He speaks His mercy into us through that same opened gate of grace. And in turn, the soul speaks within itself with **God** through that same open gate: and in such inward speaking, it is fed and refreshed by **God’s** out-speaking <note>original: "Außsprechen"; the divine Word or expression of God's essence into the soul.</note>, and is also enlightened and renewed.

For it eats from the out-breathing <note>original: "Außhauchen"; the Holy Spirit or the living breath of God.</note> of **God**, which has become human as the flesh and blood of **Christ**, in the same manner and way as a plant eats the sun’s power into itself, by which it is tinctured <term>tinctured: an alchemical term used here to mean infused with a new spiritual quality or essence, like a dye or a medicine.</term>, becoming balmy and good, so that it grows and blooms: So also does the soul from the Divine Sun, from which it becomes light and powerful.

This is now the nut and fruit of right praying: which nut no external mouth and no will turned away from **God** may reach; but only the one who has turned inward, who surrenders himself entirely to **God**.

### Concerning Holy Prayer

If such a thing is to happen, the will must turn away from all other creatures <note>In Böhme’s time, "creatures" referred to all created things—people, objects, and worldly distractions—rather than just animals.</note> and from all earthly things, standing purely before **GOD**. In this state, the business of the creatures, or those temporal things for which one wishes to ask **GOD**, should only follow in the flesh and remain behind the pure will. This ensures that the pure will brings the body’s necessities before **GOD** while the flesh itself, with its desires, does not interfere; otherwise, it introduces earthly lust into the divine, blessed working.

Therefore, right and earnest prayer—if we wish to obtain anything from **GOD**—always requires true repentance <note>original: "Busse"; this implies a complete inward turning or "change of mind" away from the self and toward God.</note> and inward humility. For praying rightly is a taking of that which the soul desires, of which **Christ** says:
> From now on the kingdom of heaven suffers violence, and those who do violence take it by force. (Matthew 11:12)

For this reason, I will provide a short formula <note>original: "Formulam"; a Latin term for a prescribed form of words used in a ritual or prayer.</note> for a confession or preparation, showing how a person should prepare themselves beforehand when they wish to bring their short prayers and requests before **GOD**.

For one may be heard as well in a short prayer as with many words, provided that the heart stands rightly before **GOD**. It does not require long words, but only a faithful, repentant soul that surrenders itself with all earnestness into the mercy of **GOD**, into **GOD's** compassion; for a single sigh
