## The Second Point.

As we now wish to describe how the <term>Principles [original: *Principia*, the three fundamental levels of reality]</term> unite with one another, we must place fire, as the highest strength, in the center. This gives to each Principle a pleasing life and to a spirit the nature it desires. Therefore, there is no conflict within the Principles, for fire is the life of all Principles; it holds the cause of life, but not life itself. To the abyss, it gives its "woe" as a sting, so that death may find itself within a life; otherwise, the abyss would be a mere silence. It gives to the abyss its <term>wrath [original: *Grimm*, referring to a fierce, energetic force]</term>, which is the life, mobility, and <term>original source [original: *Urstand*]</term> of the abyss; otherwise, it would be a silent eternity and a nothingness.

To the Light-World, fire also gives its essence; otherwise, there would be no perception or light within it, and everything would be only one—yet outside of the fire, it would be a nothingness, like an "eye of wonders" that does not know itself because no original source was within it, but rather an eternal hiddenness, where no seeking or accomplishing could exist.

To the <term>Third Principle [original: *dritten Principio*]</term>, which is the kingdom of this world, fire also gives its essence and <term>drive [original: *Quaal*, a term Böhme uses to describe both the 'quality' of a thing and the 'laboring' or 'torment' that forces it into being]</term>, through which all life and growth are stirred into motion. All sensation, and whatever is ever to become something, must possess fire: nothing springs forth from the earth without the essence of fire. It is the cause of all three Principles, and of everything that can be named.

## The Second Point.

...of the three, one; so that there is no conflict between the <term>Principles [original: *Principi*]</term>. But within the <term>essence [original: *Essenz*]</term> there is conflict; this must be, or else everything would be a nothingness. <note>Böhme argues that without the friction or "strife" between opposing forces, nothing could be manifest or felt; existence requires tension.</note>

***

Only this remains for us to consider: from what does enmity originate? God has created <term>creatures [original: *Creaturen*]</term> in every Principle, according to the nature and property of that Principle, to remain within it. If they do not remain therein, but instead introduce something else into their own property through their <term>imagination [original: *imagination*]</term>, then this becomes enmity and pain for them <note>In Böhme’s thought, "imagination" is the formative power of the soul's will to shape itself.</note>—as with the Devil and fallen humanity, both of whom departed from the Light-World. The Devil entered the <term>abyss [original: *Abgrund*]</term> of the powerful force of <term>wrath [original: *Grimmes*]</term> out of pride, and humanity entered into this world, into the <term>mystery [original: *Mysterium*]</term> of much-knowledge as if into the wonders. Now humanity experiences distress and conflict, struggling to find a way out again; yet this world into which they have entered holds them fast, for it desires to possess them.

And if one should ever depart with power, the world becomes resentful toward them, strikes out at them, and will not tolerate them within itself. This is why the children of this world are hostile toward the children of light—harassing, striking, killing, and driving them away from here—for the spirit of this world drives them to do so. The Devil also assists in this, for he knows that this world stands upon the abyss, and that when this mystery is broken <note>original: *in Zerbrechung dieses Mysterii*</note>, he will gain the children of this world for his own kingdom. Therefore, he drives the children of God away from the children of this world, so that they do not lead the children of this world into the Light-World along with them.

# The Third Point.
## Chapter IV.
### On the Origin of the Conflict in Growth, in which Life Becomes At Odds with Itself.

A thing that is one, which has only one will, does not fight against itself. But where there are many wills in one thing, they become contentious, for each wishes to go its own chosen way. However, if one is master of the others and has full power over them, so that he may break them if they do not obey him, then the thing perhaps persists as a single being; the many wills all submit in obedience to their master.

Thus it is also in the conflict of life; for the...

# Chapter IV.

<meta>catchword: continues</meta>

Life exists in many wills; every <term>essence [original: *Essentz*]</term> <note>For Böhme, an "essence" is a living, active power or potential within the soul rather than a static substance.</note> may carry a will, and carries it indeed. For the Harsh, the Bitter, the Anguished, and the Sour constitute a **contrary torment**, where each has its own quality and they are entirely opposed to one another. So too, the Fire is the enemy of all the others, for it puts every torment into great anguish; thus, there is a great contrariety between them, where one is hostile to the other—as can be seen in heat and cold, or in fire and light, and in life and death.

In the same way, man’s life is at odds with itself. One <term>form [original: *Gestalt*]</term> <note>These "forms" refer to the seven fundamental properties of nature (such as attraction, friction, and fire) that Böhme believes constitute all matter and spirit.</note> is hostile to another in all creatures. This remains the case unless the form of life receives a gentle, lovely Master, under whose constraint they must remain, and who can break their power and their will. That Master is the **Light of Life**; it is the Master of all forms and can tame them all. They must all surrender their will to the Light, and they do so gladly, for the Light gives them gentleness and power, so that their rigid, harsh, bitter, and anxious forms are all transformed into loveliness. They surrender all their will to the Light of Life; the Light gives them gentleness.

In this way, the multiplicity is transformed into **One**—into a single will, which is called the <term>Mind [original: *Gemühte*]</term>. This is the **wellspring** from which the single will can draw both evil and good. This occurs through <term>Imagination</term> <note>Böhme uses "Imagination" to describe a creative, magical act of the will—the process by which the soul "images" or takes on the likeness of what it desires.</note> or through the **representation** of a thing that is either evil or good. The quality of that represented thing then becomes the quality and the capability within the life itself.

The quality of life...

[The mind] begins to catch the property of the envisioned thing—whether it be a word or a work—and ignites itself with it within itself. When this center is ignited in wrath or love, it takes hold in all seven forms of nature; these grasp at the soul’s will-spirit, in which the noble image <note>original: *Bildnuß* — the divine image of God within man.</note> stands, in which God reveals Himself, and they lead their ignited fire into it. This can be seen in fire: depending on what <term>matter [original: *Materia*]</term> it burns in, it gives off a corresponding glow, as can be recognized in sulfur compared to wood, and in many other things.

Thus one understands from this how the fire has a <term>torment</term> and a property; the light and the power of the light also receive such a property. Since our noble image of **GOD** stands in the Light of Life, in the soul-fire, it is highly recognizable to us how the soul’s will-spirit corrupts the noble image and becomes ignited in the torment of wrath, and often also in the torment of love. ### The Third Point.

...whichever essence <term>essence [original: *Essenz*]</term> gains dominion within him—whether wrath <term>wrath [original: *Grimm*]</term> or gentleness <term>gentleness [original: *Sanfftmuht*]</term>—that is what he catches, that is what clings to him and leads him, giving him his character and will, and uniting itself entirely with him. ### Chapter VI.

...ness; that which has come from the Light-World—everything is enclosed within wrath and death. And just as the divine power sets everything in motion, so that everything grows out and through the fury of death; for the earthly **tincture** <term>tincture [original: *Tinctur*]</term> <note>In Böhme’s thought, a "tincture" is a spiritual essence or life-force that gives a substance its specific qualities and power.</note> has no fellowship with the heavenly one in the Light-World. But we find another **tincture** in the earth which has fellowship with the heavenly one—as in precious metals—and yet nothing is closed off. 

We thus understand the movement and the *fiat* <term>let it be [original Latin: *fiat*]</term> <note>The "Fiat" is the creative "Word" of God; Böhme sees it as an active, shaping power that continues to work within nature.</note> within the eternal world, both the dark and the light; each yearned for substance <term>substance [original: *Wesen*]</term>, and when **God** moved for once, one world could not be moved without the other. For the dark world contains the first *center* <term>center [original Latin: *centrum*]</term> of **Nature**, and the Light-World the other *center*, namely the **Heart of God**, or the **Word** of the power of the **Godhead**, and one world is not separated from the other. 

By this we recognize the danger into which we might hurl ourselves with our will. For if we hurl ourselves into the earthly longing <term>longing [original: *Sucht*]</term> <note>The German *Sucht* implies a driving, obsessive urge or "addiction" to material existence.</note>, it captures us. Then the **torment** <term>torment [original: *Quaal*]</term> <note>Böhme often links the word *Quaal* (pain/torment) to *Quelle* (source), implying that the very source of a being's life becomes a torment if it lacks the light of God.</note> of the **abyss** is our master, and the **sun** is our temporal **God**. But if we hurl ourselves with our will into the world outside this world, then the Light-World captures our will, and **God** becomes our master; and we leave the earthly life of this world and take with us what has come into us from the Light-World—understand this as occurring in *Adam*—so that we are led out of this world with the will that becomes one spirit with **God**.

## The Fourth Point.

**Reason** says: Where then are the three worlds? It simply wants to have a separation, where one would be outside of the other, or stand above the other, which is surely not possible. Otherwise the eternal **groundless** <term>groundless [original: *ungründliche*]</term> <note>This refers to the *Ungrund*, a central concept in Böhme’s philosophy describing the absolute, indeterminate divine depth that precedes all created things and "grounds."</note> **substance** <term>substance [original: *Wesen*]</term> <note>In Böhme's vocabulary, *Wesen* means both "being" and "essential matter."</note> would have to divide itself. How can that divide itself which is in nothing (which has no place, which is itself everything)? It certainly cannot come into particulars, for it has no ground; it cannot be grasped; it dwells within itself and possesses itself; rather, it goes out from itself and reveals itself from itself. 

It makes a thing out of itself which in itself is only a **Will**. Within itself it is a **Spirit**, but it makes out of itself a **likeness** <term>likeness [original: *Gestaltnüß*]</term> of the Spirit, and the likeness makes a substance according to the **quality** <term>quality [original: *Eigenschaft*]</term> of the Spirit. As this world is then a substance, and the inner Spirit possesses it. He is in every place, yet the place does not grasp Him; rather, He grasps the place. The place knows nothing of Him, but feels Him, for He is the **power** <term>power [original: *Krafft*]</term> and the Spirit in the place. 

His will goes through the substance, and the substance has no eyes to see Him. But He is the seeing of the place, and is Himself no place or location, but makes for Himself a groundless location where there is no measure. He is everything, yet to be regarded as a nothing compared to the outer. What He gives out of Himself, He also possesses; He does not travel into it, but is already there before the substance occupies the place. The place grasps only a **glimmer** <term>glimmer [original: *Glast*]</term> <note>An archaic word for a shine, reflection, or flash of light.</note> of His will, just as one can see his form in a **mirror**, yet cannot grasp—

# The Fifth Point.
## The Seventh Chapter.
### How a life in this tree may perish. How it steps out of the torment of love and joys into a torment of misery, which is contrary to all others.

Every life is a bright luster and mirror, and looks like a flash of a terrifying sight. But when that same flash sees the light, it transforms into a gentleness and lets the terror sink, for the terror integrates itself into the light. Thus the light shines out of the terrifying flash, for the flash is the **essence** of the light; it is its fire. The flash holds within it the <term>center of nature [original: *Centrum Naturæ*]</term> <note>In Böhme’s cosmology, this is the point where the spiritual and physical forces of the universe originate.</note>, for the fourth form of nature is the flash. There life originates, which reaches perfection in the steadfast fire as if in the <term>principle [original: *Principio*]</term>, but in the light, it is placed into another **torment** <note>original: *Quaal*. Böhme often uses this word to mean both a painful struggle and a "quality" or "source-spring" (*Quelle*). Here, even joy is described as a kind of vibrant, active state or "torment."</note>.

Now, however, the origin of the <term>imagination [original: *Imagination*, meaning the soul’s creative power of desire]</term> is in the first form of nature, as in the desiring harshness; it carries its power through the dark world into the fire. # The Fifth Point.

The goal of the spirit / where it is born / it is now free / it may go back again / into its mother / the dark world / with its <term>imagination [original: *Imagination*]</term> <note>For Böhme, "Imagination" is the soul's power to "image" or desire something into being.</note>, or sink forward into the <term>fire's anguish [original: *Feuers Angst*]</term> / through death / and turn green in the light / as it wishes / it stands in its own choice / wherever it gives itself / there it must be / for its fire must have an essence / that it has to consume. In the dark quality it burns / in the dark / harsh / severe torment / and sees into itself only as a flash; it has only the mirror of darkness / and sees into the darkness / and in the light's quality it receives the gentleness of the light / in which the light-fire burns / and looks into the light-world. ### The Seventh Chapter.

Thus, the corruption of life may now be recognized / which happens in the <term>Principle [original: *Principio*]</term> <note>The "Principle" refers to the foundational state or source of a particular reality—in this case, the transition point between nature and spirit.</note>; there is the pivot / where the will may swing wherever it wishes / to be master within <term>Multiplicity [original: *Vielheit*]</term> <note>The state of many separate, conflicting things, rather than the unity of God.</note> itself; In this state, it can grasp multiplicity in no other way / than in the dark, severe <term>harshness [original: *Herbigkeit*]</term> <note>The first quality of nature in Böhme's system: a contracting, ego-centric force.</note> / in the dark world. But if it wishes to enter into the "Nothing" / into Freedom / then it must surrender itself to the fire / so it sinks into the death of the Principle / and then it greens forth out of the fire-anguish into the light; for when it surrenders / the eternal will leads it toward nature / which is **God** the Father / into himself / out through the fire; for by surrendering, it returns home to the first will of nature / which leads it, along with the other will / which is his Son or Heart / out of the <term>Anxiety-Nature [original: *Angst-Natur*]</term> / and places it with the Son’s will into Freedom / outside of the fire-torment / where instead of "Many," it receives the "Nothing" <note>By "Nothing," Böhme means the "Unground" or the absolute freedom of God that precedes all created things.</note> for its activity or power / **God** is within it as its will and doing. But whatever wishes to be master in the fire / goes into its own number / into its own essence / which it is itself; and that which gives up its power / also gives up its fire-burning / and returns home to the one / who is the cause of the fire / namely the eternal will of **God**.

Thus it has fallen into Freedom outside its torment-fire / and its fire ignites the Freedom; now it has become a light for it / and a bright mirror / for it has surrendered itself into Freedom / as into **God**. Thus its fire is a shine and radiance of the Majesty of **God**

...of **God**. But he who does not wish to surrender, but wishes instead to be his own master, remains within his own selfhood. He cannot lead himself any higher in his own forms than out of the fire, and then only as far as the flash <note>Böhme uses the term "flash" (*Blitz*) to describe the sudden transition or ignition point where the dark, contracting forces of nature strike against the desire for light.</note>; for no hell-fire can burn within him, as he has no hellish essence within him to feed the fire. This happens in the same manner as the other <term>Principle [original: *Principium*]</term> <note>The "Second Principle" in Böhme’s thought is the world of Light and Love, associated with the Son of God, which exists eternally alongside the "First Principle" of Fire/Father.</note> has ignited itself from eternity.

Thus, we understand how a life may be corrupted, and how it leads itself into darkness through anguish and torment. It happens when life wishes to be its own master and desires <term>Multiplicity [original: *Vielheit*]</term>; if nothing is willing to yield itself to death <note>Böhme frequently uses "death" as a metaphor for the mystical "dying to the self" or "Gelassenheit" (releasement), which is necessary for spiritual rebirth.</note>, then it can reach no other world. For every life arises in "anguish-torment" within nature, and has no light within itself unless it enters into that which caused nature; only there does it receive light. For everything that is within nature is dark and in anguish, as can be recognized in this world: should the sun be taken away, there would be nothing but raw anguish and darkness. Therefore, **God** moved himself to give a light to this world, so that the outer life might stand in the light. But regarding the inner life of the soul, it has a different form.

### The Fifth Point.

...and the **Soul-Fire** <note>original: *Seelen-Feuer*. Böhme views the soul as a literal spark of divine fire that needs "fuel" to burn either as light or as dark heat.</note> enters into the house of mourning, as into the center of darkness.

During the time of the external body, the soul possesses three mirrors—or eyes—of all three worlds. Toward whichever mirror the soul turns, through that one it sees. However, it possesses only one by **natural right** <note>original: *Natur-Rechte*</note>, and that is the **fire-flash** <note>original: *Feuer-Blitz*. This is Böhme’s term for the moment of ignition where life begins, sitting at the junction between darkness and light.</note>, which is the fourth property in the dark world. This is the place where the **Principle** <note>original: *Principium*</note> originates, where the two inner worlds part: one into the darkness, the other into the light. Therein lies the soul's eternal origin. Into whichever world the soul directs its will, it receives substance from that world as a **spiritual body**; for that same substance becomes a food or matter for the burning of the soul-fire.

For this reason, God has placed the soul into flesh and blood, so that it might not so easily become susceptible to the **essence of wrath** <note>original: *Grimmes Wesen*. This refers to the harsh, consuming quality of "dark nature" before it is tempered by God's love.</note>. In the meantime, the soul finds its joy in the **sun-mirror** and delights in **astral essence** <note>original: *Syderischer Essentz*. 2. And the Dark World stands in the fire-root.
3. But the external elementary world stands in **starry-torment** <note>original: *Sternen-Quaal*. The "torment" refers to the constant friction and conflicting influences of the celestial bodies on the material world.</note>; between these hovers the great mystery of the soul-fire.

### The Fifth Point.

**Reason** speaks: How is a child to blame if its parents are godless? Indeed, what can God do about it? Does it even lie within the parents' power to make a child? Why does God allow this—that harlots and scoundrels crawl together—even though the <term>false tree: *falsche Baum*; refers to a lineage or nature corrupted by sin.</term> does not only originate from this lineage alone, but also within marriage? Yet man is free; if he awakens no life, then his <term>seed: *Same*; the biological and spiritual potential for a new human life.</term> remains a mere <term>essence: *Essenz*; the inner spiritual substance or potential.</term>. But should God, for the sake of the child’s innocence, throw pearls before swine? The Kingdom of Heaven certainly stands open before it; it may enter; God shuts it to no one. But a wicked person is closed off in body and soul; why not also in the seed? For the seed is indeed the fruit of his body. If one wants to harvest good wheat, one must rightly sow wheat; but if thistle-seed is sown, a thistle grows from it. Should God then transform it into wheat? Has not the sower power to sow what he will upon his field? Or would you say: what is the thistle to blame, that it is a thistle and stings? Yet it does not belong among the wheat, even though it grows up with it. God would be well pleased if no thistle-child grew at all; for weeds are not part of His order, but rather the Devil sows them among the wheat—that is, into the <term>mind: *Gemüthe*; the deep-seated spiritual disposition or "soul-center" of a person.</term> of man. Why does man permit this, and corrupt himself, so that his essence becomes a thistle-seed, and bears weeds for the fire in the <term>Wrath: *Grimme*; the "fierceness" or dark, consuming side of God’s nature that reacts to sin.</term> of God? It does not all depend on the seed, however, but on the field.

# Chapter VIII.

Many a noble grain perishes in the <term>essence: *Essentz*; the inner spiritual substance or foundational quality of a thing.</term> of a bad field. Heaven and the sun provide life and <term>power: *Krafft*; divine virtue or vital energy.</term> to all that grows. The sun does not create <term>weeds: *Unkraut*; literally "un-herb," referring to tares or spiritually corrupt growth.</term>, nor does it desire any; however, the essences within the field often produce something else and spoil what is good. The same is true in man: many a curse remains attached when one person wishes it upon another. If the other person has provoked the curse and is susceptible to it—as is commonly the case among **godless spouses**, where one wishes the other to the Devil and to the fires of Hell.

Since they are both godless, why should their godless will not also be fulfilled, so that they beget godless children? Since there is nothing good within them, what good should come out of them? What can God do about this? He places His Word and teaching before them and announces their destruction <note>original: *Verderben*; can also mean perdition or ruin.</note>; if they do not want it, they go where they wish to go. Such also is their **seed**, and thus many a child is born a thistle or a wild beast, and is baptized in the **Wrath of God**. For in whatever essence the spirit of the soul resides, in such an essence it also receives the Divine Being within the covenant—one in the power of the light and in love, the other in the power of fury <note>original: *Grimmes*; referring to the "dark" or "wrathful" side of the divine fire.</note> and in **darkness**. The covenant of **Baptism** remains: every child is baptized within the covenant; the Spirit of God baptizes everyone, provided the custom is observed, but according to the child's own quality. Often, father and mother, and even the one performing the baptism, are godless and

## Chapter X.

### Of the four elements of the devil and the dark world / how one shall recognize them in this external world.

The first element of the dark world and of the devil is pride, the second is greed, the third is envy, the fourth is wrath. These four elements always and eternally hatch a young son, who is named Falsehood. This same son is also a true son of the corrupted Adam, whom he left behind to be a master of the world; he has become king in the world, and has possessed the entire world, and reigns in all places in the third <term>Principle: *Principio*; in Böhme’s cosmology, the "Third Principle" is the visible, material world which emerged from the tension between the spiritual worlds of light and darkness</term>. Whoever truly knows this king, knows the four elements of the devil; for in the dark world these four elements have the entire dominion, in spirit and body, and in everything that is called <note>original: "Wesen" - can mean being, essence, or substance</note> existence.

And we see clearly from this, that this external world stands upon the foundation of these same four elements, and receives its inclination from them, as well as its torment and its will; for the son of these same four elements reigns upon earth; he wants to have everything under his obedience, and has many kinds of his subjects.

1. The generation of pride, which wants to be above all others, and does not want to be equal.

<summary>Böhme identifies the four "elements" of the demonic realm—pride, greed, envy, and wrath—which together produce "Falsehood," the ruling spirit of the fallen material world. He explains that these forces govern human society and the physical realm, with pride acting as the primary drive for those seeking power over others.</summary>

### The Tenth Chapter.

[we] <note>The text begins mid-sentence; based on context, it refers to how we must live as true Christians.</note> should always desire to do good—not out of **pride**, **greed**, **envy**, or **wrath**, but in **humility**, doing good with a sincere heart. # J. B. <note>These initials refer to Jacob Böhme (1575–1624), a German mystic and theologian whose work deeply influenced Western esotericism.</note>

# Of the Mixed World and Its Wickedness.

## Is a Mirror, in which everyone can behold themselves and examine: Whose spirit’s child they are.

CHRIST says, Matthew 23: O Jerusalem, Jerusalem: How often I wanted to gather your children, as a clucking hen <note>original: "Gluck-Henne"; a maternal image of God common in Böhme’s writing to illustrate divine care.</note> gathers her chicks under her wings, and you would not. What does it profit you to indulge in worldly pleasure <note>original: *Wollust*, referring to sensual indulgence or luxury</note> for a little while, resulting in eternal shame? You think you love them and are doing them good; when the world praises their cunning, luxury, and falsehood, that pleases you well. But the Devil accepts this, and you are your children’s murderer; you are their greatest enemy. For children look to their parents; when parents are pleased by their antics <note>original: *Possen*, referring to worldly follies or foolish behaviors</note>, they carry them out all the more and are all the bolder. They will cry out against their parents at the Last Judgment, because they did not turn them away from luxury and a godless life toward discipline and the fear of God.

   Do you love your life and your children? Then lose them to the wickedness of this world, so that they do not exist and walk within it; thus you shall find them, along with your life, in heaven...

For a serious Christian does not even truly know himself: he sees nothing but his own lack of virtue <note>original: *Untugend*, referring to vices or moral failings</note>, in which the devil fights against him; this is always before him. But his holiness he does not recognize in this world: for Christ hides it under his cross <note>In the original text, the author uses the symbol "+" to represent the Cross of Christ.</note>, so that the devil does not see it. Therefore, be awake and alert at all times, and resist the cunning devil, so that you may live eternally, AMEN.

# Epistle to a Good Friend
## By Jacob Böhme.

-> Our salvation in the active love of JESUS CHRIST within us. <-

My very dear and Christian Lord, high peace, along with a heartfelt, brotherly <note>original: *gliedtlicher*, literally "memberly," referring to being members of the Body of Christ</note>—and in the desire for active love—wishing that for the Lord, the true Sun of the effective <note>original: *würcklichen*, meaning active or working</note> love of Jesus Christ may continually rise and shine in soul, spirit, and body.

Your letter, dated the 24th of January <term>January</term>, I received fourteen days after Easter <term>Easter</term>, and I rejoiced in it, for I see therein that the Lord is a hungry, zealous, and eager seeker and lover of the true Ground <note>Böhme uses the word *Grund* (Ground) to refer to the fundamental reality or origin of all being</note>; which, as I understand, the Lord has diligently sought after and explored.

But that my writings have also come into your hands and that you find pleasure in them, that is certainly the cause and a Divine Order, which leads those who love toward Love, and often uses strange means through which He fulfills the desire of those who love, through which He feeds them with His gift, and introduces into their love an Essence <term>Ens</term> <note>Latin for 'being' or 'essence'; in Böhme’s terminology, this refers to a spiritual substance or nourishment</note> to burn as a true fire: And the Lord should certainly believe, as long as he remains constant in the love of the truth, that it will open itself to him in fire-flaming love and make itself known rightly. Only let it be started correctly: For it is not through our sharp reason and searching that we attain the true Ground of Divine Knowledge. The search must begin from within, in the hunger of the soul: For the inquiry of reason goes only as far as its Star <term>Astrum</term> <note>A term referring to the 'astral' or celestial influences that Böhme believed governed the physical world and the human intellect</note> of the outer world, from which reason originates. But the soul searches in its own Star <term>Astrum</term>, as in the internal spiritual world, from which the visible world arose or flowed forth, and in which the soul stands with its Ground.

But if the soul wishes to search its own Star, as the Great Mystery <term>Mysterium Magnum</term> <note>A central concept in Böhme's philosophy, referring to the "Great Mystery" or the chaotic womb of all possibilities from which the universe was created</note>, it must first entirely surrender all its power and will to Divine Love and Grace, and first become as a child, and through great repentance, turn toward its Center <term>Centro</term> <note>The inward point of contact between the soul and the Divine</note>, and wish to do nothing except what the Spirit of God wishes to search through it. And when it has so surrendered itself, and thereby seeks nothing but God and its own salvation, together with the service and love of its neighbor, and finds itself then in such a desire that it would gladly have Divine and Natural Knowledge, then it should know that it is from

<meta>catchword: God</meta>

God is drawn into it, then the soul may well search such a deep Ground <note>Böhme uses "Ground" (*Grund*) to refer to the fundamental, unmanifested essence of God and reality</note> as is indicated in my writings.

For the Spirit of God searches through the soul and leads it finally into the depth of the Deity, as St. Paul says: *The Spirit searches all things, even the depth of the Deity.* <note>Reference to 1 Corinthians 2:10: "The Spirit searches all things, even the deep things of God."</note>

My dear Lord, it is quite a simple children's way to the highest wisdom; the world does not know it. You do not need to seek it in far-off places. It stands at your soul's door and knocks. If it can find a vacant, surrendered <term>Gelassenheit</term> <note>A central term in German mysticism meaning "yieldedness" or "letting go" of the self-will to allow God to act</note> place in the soul, it will reveal itself there and rejoice more within it than the sun does in the elements. If the soul gives itself over to Wisdom as its property, then Wisdom penetrates the soul with its fire-flaming love and unlocks all mysteries to it.

It might perhaps cause the Lord to wonder: how is it that a layman could understand such high things? One who has never learned nor read them. But I tell you, my dear Lord, that until now you have seen only a glimmer of such mysteries in my writings. For one cannot write it down: if you were recognized by God as worthy so that the Light would be kindled in your soul, you would hear, taste, smell, feel, and see unspeakable words of God from such knowledge. Only then is it the true **Theosophical Pentecost-School**: where the soul is taught by God.

<margin>1</margin> After this, there is no need for searching or sharp labor: all the gates stand open. Even a very simple person can come to it, if he only does not resist it with his own willing and running. For it already lies within man; it only needs to be awakened by God's Spirit.

In my **Talent** <note>original: *Talento*; Böhme refers to his spiritual gift or the "talents" bestowed by God in the biblical parable</note>, as I have been able to write it down in my simplicity, you will well see the way to this; especially in this attached booklet, which is also a product of my talent and was only sent to print a few weeks ago. I present this to the Lord in love as my Christian fellow-member, and I exhort him to read through it often: for its virtue is called "the longer, the dearer" <note>original: *je länger je lieber*, a common German idiom for something that becomes more precious over time</note>. In this booklet, the Lord will see a true, brief Ground which is certain; for the author has experienced it in **practice** <note>original Latin: *praxi*</note>.

As for what concerns the Ground of the high natural mysteries—of which the Lord desires more illustration alongside Mr. Walter <note>Balthasar Walther, a physician and close associate of Böhme</note> and Mr. Leonhard Elver—may he inquire with Mr. Walter about it. For I have sent an explanation to you and to him, alongside other new writings; if they please you, you may have them copied. You will find very great knowledge within them.

I wish / that you may all understand this rightly. I would also like to provide it even more simply / but because of the great depth / and then also for the sake of the unworthy / it may not happen now. Christ says: <note>original: "Matt. 7.v.7. If you will take right heed of this / then my writings will give you great occasion and instruction therein / and the Sign-Star <note>Likely referring to the "Star of the Signature" or a celestial omen Böhme associated with the dawn of a new spiritual era</note> over your Pole will help you / for its time is born. Let no one gape any longer for the time / it is already born / whom it hits, it hits / he who wakes / sees it / and he who sleeps / sees it not. It has appeared / the time / and will soon appear / he who wakes / sees it. Many have already felt it: But first a great tribulation must pass by / before it becomes entirely manifest. That will become manifest / therefore no godly man should defile himself with such bickering: There is a fire from the Lord in it / which will burn him / and reveal the truth itself.

What more there is / he shall receive from Mr. Walter / especially a table <note>Referring to a "Tabula," a diagram or symbolic chart illustrating Böhme's complex theological system</note> together with the explanation / in which the whole Ground is set before the eyes. And I commend the Lord to the love of Jesus Christ. Dated the 20th of April / In the year 1624. <note>original: "Anno 1624"</note>

->The Lord's in the love of Christ<-
->Obediently<-
->Jacob Böhme.<-

# Explanation of several words in the writings of J. B. <note>Jacob Böhme often used a specialized vocabulary to describe his mystical visions; this section serves as a glossary for readers.</note>

## THE GREAT TURBA <note>original: "TURBA MAGNA." From the Latin for "great commotion" or "uproar." In Böhme’s thought, it represents a state of chaos or the awakening of divine wrath within nature.</note>

This is the stirred up and awakened wrath of the inner ground / where the Hellish Foundation / becomes manifest in the spirit of the world: from which great plagues and diseases arise. It is also the awakened wrath of outer nature / as can be seen in the terror of great storms / where the fire becomes manifest in the water. In short / it is a pouring out of God’s wrath / by which nature is disturbed <note>original: "turbirt"</note>.

### Ternary <note>original: "Ternarius." Referring to a grouping of three or a threefold manifestation.</note>

In the word Ternary, one understands in the Language of Nature <note>Böhme believed in a "Language of Nature" (*Natursprache*) where the sounds of words revealed the inner essence of the things they named.</note> / precisely the Divine Birth in 6 Forms in nature / which are 6 Seals of God.

### Holy Ternary <note>original: "Ternarius Sanctus."</note>

This is the inner Heavenly working Power in the Essence / in which the Trinity of God works: and thus I understand an essential power / and the number 3 in seven forms / in which the Angelic World <note>original: "Englische Welt." In this context, "Englische" refers to angels (*Engel*), not the English nation.</note> is included.

## THE THREE PRINCIPLES <note>original: "TRIA PRINCIPIA." This is Böhme’s central framework for reality: 1. The Dark World (Fire/Wrath), 2. The Light World (Love/Majesty), and 3. The Outer World (the physical universe).</note>

### 1st Principle

With the 1st Principle / is indicated / the eternal darkness / which consists in the attractions of the properties / from which sensitivity originates: and it reaches with its ground into the fire. Therein one perceives the Eternal Nature and the wrath of God.

<meta>catchword: 2. Prin-</meta>

<meta>This page concludes a prophetic letter from Böhme, dated just months before his death in 1624. I wish that you all might correctly understand all of this. I would gladly present it even more simply; however, because of the great depth, and also for the sake of the unworthy, it may not happen now. Christ says in Matthew 7:7: Seek, and you shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you. No man can give this to another; each must obtain it for himself from God. One can certainly give guidance to another, but he cannot give him the understanding itself.

## However, know that a lily blooms for you in the northern lands. <note>original: "Mitternächtigen Ländern." Literally "midnight lands," a term Böhme and his contemporaries used for Northern Europe. The "Lily" is Böhme’s signature symbol for a future age of spiritual renewal and peace.</note>

If you do not destroy this lily yourselves through the sectarian quarreling of the scholars, it will become a great tree among you. But if you would rather quarrel than recognize the true God, then the ray of light will pass you by and strike only a few; thereafter, you will have to fetch water for the soul's thirst from foreign peoples. If you take this correctly to heart, my writings will provide you with great occasion and instruction for it, and the Star of Signature <note>original: "Signat-Stern." This refers to Böhme’s doctrine of the *Signatura Rerum*, or the "Signature of All Things," where the outward appearance of a thing reveals its inner divine character.</note> above your pole will help you, for its time is now born. I will gladly give you what the Lord has given me, but you must take it up and apply it rightly; it will be a testimony for you against the mockers. No one should look upon my person; this is a pure gift of God, not only for my sake, but for yours, and for all those who come to read it. Let no one gape any longer for the time to come; it is already born. Whomever it hits, it hits; he who is awake sees, and he who sleeps sees nothing. The time has appeared, and will soon appear fully; he who is awake sees it. Many have already felt it, but a great tribulation <note>A likely reference to the suffering of the Thirty Years' War (1618–1648), which Böhme viewed as a period of divine purification.</note> must first pass by before it becomes entirely manifest. This is the cause: the strife of the learned, who trample Christ’s cup with their feet and quarrel over a child who has never been more wicked since humanity began. This shall become manifest; therefore, no pious man should defile himself with such quarreling. There is a fire from the Lord within it, which will burn the quarrel away and reveal the Truth itself.

Whatever else remains will be received from Master Walter <note>Balthasar Walther (1558–1631), a physician and traveled scholar who was a close friend and patron of Böhme.</note>, especially the table along with the explanation, in which the entire foundation is placed before one's eyes. And I commend the Master to the love of Jesus Christ. Dated the 20th of April, in the year 1624.

->The Lord’s in the love of Christ,<-
->Your servant,<-
->Jacob Böhme.<-

<meta>This page begins a glossary titled "Explanation of certain words," intended to help readers navigate the dense, symbolic terminology of Jacob Böhme’s mystical writings. It follows the preceding letter’s conclusion where Böhme urged his readers to seek internal understanding of the "Signature of All Things."</meta>

# Explanation of certain words in the writings of J. B. <note>J. B. refers to the author, Jacob Böhme.</note>

## THE GREAT TURMOIL <note>original: "TURBA MAGNA." In Böhme’s thought, the *Turba* is the disruptive, destructive power that arises when the elements of nature fall out of harmony with the divine order.</note>

This is the stirred and awakened wrath of the inner ground, where the hellish foundation becomes manifest in the spirit of the world: from which great plagues and illnesses arise. It is also the awakened wrath <note>original: "Grimm." This refers to the "fierceness" or "severity" of God’s nature when separated from His love.</note> of the outer nature, as can be seen in the shower of great thunderstorms, when the fire becomes manifest in the water. In short, it is an outpouring of God’s wrath, by which nature is disturbed.

## The Triad <note>original: "Ternarius," a Latin term for a group of three.</note>

In the word *Triad*, one understands in the Language of Nature <note>The "Language of Nature" (*Natursprache*) is Böhme’s concept of a mystical language where the sound of a word reveals the true essence of the thing named.</note> the true Divine birth in six forms in nature, which are the six seals of God.

## The Holy Triad <note>original: "Ternarius Sanctus."</note>

This is the inner, heavenly, active power in the essence, in which the Trinity of God works: and thus I understand it as an essential power, and the number three in seven forms, by which the angelic world <note>original: "Englische Welt." In this context, "englisch" derives from *Engel* (angel) and refers to the celestial realm of angels, not the nation of England.</note> is also included.

## THE THREE PRINCIPLES <note>original: "TRIA PRINCIPIA." These are the three foundational realms of Böhme's reality: the dark world of fire/wrath, the light world of love/spirit, and the outer visible world.</note>

### The First Principle <note>original: "1. Principium."</note>

With the first principle is indicated the eternal darkness, which consists in the receptivity of properties from which sensitivity <note>original: "Empfindlichkeit," the capacity to feel or perceive.</note> originates: and it reaches with its ground into the fire. In this, one understands Eternal Nature and the wrath of God.

<summary>This page serves as a glossary for Jacob Böhme's mystical terminology, defining concepts like the "Great Turmoil" (divine wrath in nature) and the "Triad" (divine manifestation).</summary>
<keywords>Jacob Böhme, Turba Magna, Ternarius, Holy Triad, Three Principles, Language of Nature, divine wrath, angelic world</keywords>

--- Page 852 ---
<meta>This page continues the glossary of Jacob Böhme’s mystical terminology. Having previously defined the "Turba" and the "Triad," the text now moves into the Three Principles that structure Böhme’s universe and explains the spiritual significance of the Tincture, Christ, and Satan.</meta>

### 2. The Second Principle <note>original: "2. Principium." Böhme organizes the cosmos into three "Principles": the dark fire-world (the first), the light-world of love (the second), and the physical world (the third).</note>

By the second principle is understood the Light with the Angelic Power-World <note>original: "Englischen Krafft-Welt." As noted previously, "Englisch" here refers to the nature of angels (*Engel*), not the English language or nation.</note>, wherein the outflow of Divine power and will reveals itself through the Magic fire in the Light with the fire-flaming love; therein one understands the Kingdom of God.

### 3. The Third Principle <note>original: "3. Principium."</note>

By the third principle is understood the visible elemental world with its hosts, which is an outflow from the 1st and 2nd principles through the movement and out-breathing of Divine power and will; wherein the Spiritual world—according to both light and darkness—is imaged and has entered into creaturely <note>original: "Creatürliche Art." This refers to the state of being a created thing or a "creature" within the physical realm.</note> nature.

### Tincture <note>original: "Tinctur." In alchemy, a tincture is a substance that can transform or "color" other materials. For Böhme, it represents the life-giving, transformative power that flows from the union of fire and light.</note>

By the word Tincture is understood the power of the fire and light, and the movement of this power is called the Holy or Pure Element.

## CHRIST

By the word Christ is also indicated the New Man in the spirit of Christ, understood according to the inwardness <note>original: "Inwendigkeit." This signifies the inner spiritual reality of a person as opposed to their outward, worldly appearance.</note>.

## SATAN

By the word Satan is indicated the erring spirit <note>original: "Irrgeist." A spirit that has wandered away from the divine order.</note>, and not always a creaturely devil, but rather the torment <note>original: "Quaal." Often translated as "quality" or "source" in Böhme’s unique etymology, but here primarily meaning the suffering or "source-pang" of the spirit.</note> of such an erring spirit.

->T H E   E N D.<-

# PREFACE

## To the Reader of these Writings.

<image-desc>A large ornamental drop cap 'E' featuring intricate foliate and scrollwork designs within a square border.</image-desc>

> It is written: The natural man understands nothing of the things of the Spirit, nor of the mystery of the Kingdom of God; it is a folly to him, and he cannot grasp it. <note>This is a paraphrase of 1 Corinthians 2:14, a foundational verse for Böhme’s argument that spiritual truths require spiritual rather than just intellectual eyes.</note>

Therefore, I would have the Christian lover of mysteries <note>original: "Geheimnuſſen." In Böhme’s context, this refers to the hidden inner workings of God and the cosmos.</note> be warned: if he intends to apply himself to these high writings—to read, search, and understand them—he must not read from the outside with sharp speculation and meditation. Otherwise, he will remain only in the external, figurative ground <note>original: "Grunde." For Böhme, the "Ground" (Grund) or "Unground" (Ungrund) refers to the absolute foundation or essence of being.</note> and attain nothing more than a superficial color <note>original: "gemachte Farbe," literally "made color," implying a surface-level appearance or a conceptual imitation rather than the true essence.</note> from it. For one’s own reason <note>original: "Vernunfft." Böhme often contrasts human "reason" (intellect) with "understanding" (divine insight).</note> without **God’s** light cannot reach the Ground; it is entirely impossible for it. No matter how high and subtle the <term>Natural Talent <note>original Latin: "Ingenium," referring to innate intellectual ability or wit.</note></term> may be, it still only grasps a reflection of it, as in a mirror. For **Christ** says: Without me, you can do nothing. **Likewise** <note>original Latin: "Item," a common marker in early modern texts to introduce a new point or quotation.</note>: He is the light of the world and the life of mankind.

If anyone wishes to search the Divine Ground as a Divine Revelation, he should first consider to what end he desires to know such things, and whether he also desires to practice <note>original: "practiciren," meaning to put into spiritual or ethical action.</note> that which he might attain.

## How God should be contemplated outside of nature and creation.

<image-desc>Decorative drop cap 'M' with intricate scrollwork and foliage.</image-desc>Moses says: The Lord our God is one God: And in another place it stands: Of him / through him and in him are all things. Likewise: Is it not I / who fills all things? Likewise: By his Word all things were made / that which is made. Answer: There would remain that same eternal unity / from which nature and creation received their origin. So also when I think: What is many hundred thousand miles above the stars / or what is in that place where no creature exists? A characteristic Böhme term implying both the origin and the fundamental state of being.</note></term> / there is no ground / time or place there / and it is the only GOD / or the only Good / that cannot be expressed in words.

# Further Consideration / How This One 
# GOD is Threefold.

Holy Scripture indicates to us that this One God is Threefold <note>original: "Dreyfaltig." Refers to the Trinity—the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.</note>, as a single Threefold **Being**, that has three kinds of activity, and yet is only a single Being; just as one can see this in the flowed-out power <note>This "flowed-out power" refers to the concept of emanation, where the physical world is seen as an expression of God’s internal energy.</note> in all things, if one perceives it. 

Specifically, an image is found in **Fire**, **Light**, and **Air**, which are three kinds of activities, and yet are only a single ground and being. And as one sees that fire, light, and air arise from a candle—though the candle is none of these three things, and yet is the cause of them—so also is the eternal **Unity** the cause and the ground of the eternal **Trinity**, which reveals itself out of the Unity itself, and leads into a Wanting or **Will**, **Desire**, and **Proceeding**. <note>original: "Außgang." Also translated as "Out-going" or "Emanation."</note>

The **Wanting** or **Will** is the **Father**, as the revelation or movement of the Unity, by which the Unity wills itself.

The **Desire** <note>original: "Lust." In Böhme’s writing, this does not mean "lust" in the modern sense, but rather a holy delight, joy, or the divine longing that leads to creation.</note> is the **Son**, as that which the Will wills—His love and pleasure—as is to be seen at the baptism of Christ, where the Father testified: *Matthew 3:17. This is my dear Son, in whom I am well pleased; hear Him.*

The **Desire** is the **Simplicity** <note>original: "Einfältigkeit." This refers to a state of being "single-fold" or "without division," characterizing the pure, undivided nature of the divine intention.</note> of the Will, where the Will in the Unity [shapes itself] into an activity and place of its...

## Of the Eternal Word of GOD.

Holy Scripture says: **GOD made all things through his Word**. Also: **The Word was God** (John 1). This is understood as follows:

The **Word** is nothing other than the **exhaling Will** out of the **Power** <note>original: "Krafft." In Böhme's thought, this represents the potential energy or divine essence within the Godhead.</note>; a **distinction** <note>original: "Schiedligkeit." The process of making the one into the many.</note> of the Power into a **multiplicity of powers**; a division and outflow of the **Unity**, from which **Knowledge** <note>original: "Wissenschafft." For Böhme, this does not mean "science" in the modern sense, but the active self-awareness or "knowing" that arises when the Divine reflects upon itself.</note> originates. For in a single **Being** <note>original: "Wesen."</note> in which there is no distinction and which is only one, there is no Knowledge; for even if there were, it would only know one thing: itself. But when it divides and separates from itself, the separating Will enters into **multiplicity**, and each separate part works within itself.

However, because the **Unity** cannot be torn apart or move away from itself, the division remains within the **exhaling Will** within the Unity. This division of the **Breath** provides only **distinctions**, through which the **eternal Will**—along with the **Delight** <note>original: "Lust." Refers to the divine joy or the holy longing that initiates creation.</note> and the **Proceeding**—enters into the Knowledge of the infinite forms or understanding, as into a

<summary>Böhme argues that the Trinity's movement is essential for existence, as a static Unity would result in a formless "Nothing." He describes the Word of God as a divine "exhalation" that creates the distinctions and self-awareness necessary for the multiplicity of the world.</summary>

## Of the holy Name JEHOVAH.

The ancient Rabbis among the Jews understood this to some extent, for they said this Name is the Most High Name of GOD, through which one understands the actual Godhead in a sensory way <note>original: "im sensu." These are Böhme's foundational terms: the "Ground" is the basis of existence, while the "Ungrund" or "Abyss" is the bottomless, preceding nothingness from which God emerges into self-awareness.</note>; for it is GOD himself, as the Divine, actual Sensitivity, Findability <note>original: "Findlichkeit." The quality of being "findable" or manifest to perception.</note>, Knowledge, and Love—as the true Primal State <note>original: "Urstand."</note> in the actual Unity, from which the five senses of true life spring forth.

Each letter in this Name indicates a power and special effect, as a form within the working Power. ## of Nature.

There, the masculine and feminine nature arose in the spirit of the outward world: the masculine in the fiery Mercury and the feminine in the watery. This separation occurred everywhere through everything, and to this end: that the fiery Mercury should long again for the watery, and the watery for the fiery, so that a desire of love might exist between them in the light of nature, from which their union arose. Thus, the fiery Mercury, as the outflowing Word, divided itself according to the fiery and watery light-nature; and from this now comes the masculine and feminine nature of all things, both in the living and the growing.

On the third day’s work, the fiery and watery Mercury entered again into conjunction <term>Conjunction: From the Latin *conjunctio*; refers to the alchemical "marriage" or union of opposing elements.</term> or mingling, and they received one another. Then the saltpeter <term>Saltpeter: original "Salniter." Here it refers to a vital, crystalline essence or the "spiritual earth" that provides the energetic foundation for physical growth.</term>, as the separation of the earth, gave birth to grass, herbs, and trees, and the first birthing between masculine and feminine nature took place.

God is the Eternal Unmeasurable/incomprehensible Unity, who reveals Himself in Himself from eternity to eternity, with the Trinity <term>Dreyheit: The Trinity; Böhme describes the Godhead not just as a person, but as a dynamic process of three "operations" or "workings."</term>, and is a Father, Son, and Spirit in three kinds of operation, as previously mentioned.

The first outflow and revelation of this Trinity is the **Eternal Word**, or the speaking-forth of Divine Power; the first spoken-forth essence out of the Power is the **Divine Wisdom** <note>Also known as Sophia, the mirror of God's glory through which He envisions all possibilities of being.</note> as an essence in which the Power works.

Out of the Wisdom, the power of the breathing-forth <note>original: "Außhauchens"; the divine expiration or "sigh" that initiates creation.</note> flows out and enters into **differentiation** and **forming**; therein the Divine Power becomes manifest in its virtue <note>original: "Tugend"; here used in the archaic sense of inherent power or medicinal strength.</note>.

These same differentiated powers introduce themselves into receptivity, toward their own sensitivity, and out of this sensitivity arises **self-will** and **desire**.

This self-will is the ground of eternal nature; it introduces itself with desire into properties, even unto the fire.

In the desire, **darkness** arises, and in the fire, the eternal unity is revealed with the light in the fire-burning nature.

From this fire-burning and light-nature’s kind and property, the **angels** and **souls** have originated, as a Divine Revelation.

The power of the fire and light is called **Tincture** <term>Tinctur: In alchemy, a substance that can transform or "color" another. In Böhme’s theology, it is the vital spiritualizing power that bridges the gap between the fire of God's wrath and the light of His love.</term>,

->Table of Principles<-
<note>original Latin: "Tabula Principiorum"</note>

This table, divided into seven spaces, is the foundation of the angels and souls—the Great Mystery <note>Latin: *Mysterium Magnum*, the source of all manifestation</note> of transformation, in which all possibilities reside. Across these seven numbers, one understands the outflowing of the One into the Seven. The first Principle <note>Latin: *Principium*</note> is to be understood as reaching up to the fire, where the light is revealed; and from the fire to the essence <note>German: *Wesen*</note> is the second Principle. Looking downward through the various workings <note>German: *Geschafft*, referring here to the qualities or manifestations of nature</note>, one understands what kind of outflow comes from each property through the influence of the others. It is not to be understood that a single property produces such an outflow alone; rather, all seven do so, but the first "form" <note>German: *Gestalt*</note> dominates within it and holds the chief command.

Where Number 1 stands—**Desire** or **Encompassing**—one sees that Desire is **magnetic**, for it encloses and darkens itself. This is the foundation of both eternal and temporal darkness. From such a drawing-in comes sharpness, harshness, and hardness, which are the primal state <term>Urstand: Böhme's term for the original, underlying condition or source of a thing</term> of fury, from which the great eternal <unclear>Wrath</unclear> originates; for this "magnet" pulls the power into itself. Thus, the active working stands still and enters into a state of impotence, as can be seen downward under Number (1).

Under Number (2) stands **Science** <note>Latin: *Scientz*, used here to mean an inner "knowing" or the reactive "spark" of motion within a quality</note> or **Pulling**. This is the second form of nature, namely the movement caused by the magnetic drawing-in. From this, the sensitivity of nature originates, and it is the foundation of all contrariety <note>Latin: *Contrarietät*, referring to the conflict of opposing forces necessary for life and consciousness to exist</note>.

No. 3. stands as the third form of Nature and is called **Anguish** <note>German: *Angst*. And since there could be no revelation within the unity without movement, the Divine Will flows out from itself and introduces the Divine Delight <note>German: *Lust*, here meaning a joyous inclination or pleasure</note> into the out-flowing will through desire and movement, leading toward a sensitivity <note>German: *Empfindlichkeit*, the capacity to feel or perceive oneself</note>, so that it may perceive itself.

Within this, **God** calls Himself a loving **God**, specifically according to the sensitive Divine Love-Delight; and an angry **God**, according to the cause of sensitivity, which is the eternal nature. What, then, do those toward midday <note>the South</note> do? They have fallen asleep in the heat, but a storm-wind will awaken them; during this, many will be terrified unto death. What, then, do those in the morning <note>the East</note> do? You are a proud bride from the beginning. The crown has always been offered to you from the start; but you previously thought yourself too beautiful: you live with the others.

# Chapter V.

[...The] <term>Mystery<note>original: *Mysterium*; referring to the hidden, divine reality or the "Great Secret" of God’s plan.</note></term> has entered into the wonders, for he is God’s preacher. And after the <term>Turba<note>A specific term in Böhme’s theosophy referring to the "disturber" or the spirit of divine wrath and chaos that breaks the harmony of nature.</note></term> has overcome the world, he must remain silent until the six seals have ended their wonders and the angels of the Turba have poured out their vials; then the wonders of wrath are fulfilled. 

So Enoch comes again out of the Mystery and goes into the Mystery, and tells what has happened, and rebukes the world for the sake of the Turba—because they allowed the abomination to enter into themselves and did not resist it. And after the world becomes too fat and wanton in the golden year, seeking Sodom and Gomorrah once more, then their Turba also becomes fat and wanton, seeking the wrath and the final limit. Then the golden time passes away and is swallowed up in the Turba; and then Methuselah, the oldest man, dies, and the Deluge comes in fire. Ponder this; it is a serious matter. 

We do not say that you will lay hold of Enoch with your fists; no. Enoch does not preach from the spirit of earthly life, but from that spirit which was a prophet, which led the outward man into the <term>Principle<note>original: *Principium*; in Böhme’s system, this refers to one of the three fundamental realms of existence: the dark fire-world, the light world, or the external world of nature.</note></term>. Thus, you will not touch the outward Enoch, but you will hear the prophet who speaks out of Enoch from the Mystery.

### Chapter VII.

God does not trust in splendor and pride <term>Hochmuht; a state of arrogant superiority</term>; therefore you rely on greed <term>Geitz; specifically a grasping avarice</term> and wish only to devour the fat of the earth for yourself; you take it with violence and not with right. The "right" that you follow was devised by your false, greedy heart; you live only in deception. You persuade and deceive yourself to your own harm. If you were wise <note>original: *witzig*; in this historical context, the word means mentally sharp or discerning rather than humorous</note>, you would look toward your end and what follows after this; but you blind yourself with vanity <term>Hoffart; an ostentatious or puffed-up pride</term> and yet you say: "Behold, the golden time! Many would have wished to see what we see, and hear what we hear, and they have not seen nor heard it."

Indeed, listen, for it will also be a testimony against you and make your judgment all the heavier. Until now, you have not become better, but worse; therefore know that what has been proclaimed to you was your own prophet <note>referring to a divine messenger or the internal conscience that warns of coming judgment</note>, who called you back from your vanity into the Mother of Humility <term>Demut; the humble submission of the soul to God's will</term>. 

But you have only become worse and have broken the sword of the Spirit so that you may do whatever you want. But it has abandoned you and handed you over to the **Turba** <term>Turba; in Jakob Böhme’s theology, the "Turba" is the awakening of God’s wrath or the spirit of chaos that destroys that which has fallen away from the divine order</term>, which shall devour you, as happened to Israel in ancient times. # Chapter VII.

God does not trust in pomp and pride <term>Hochmuht; an inward spirit of arrogance or over-estimation of oneself</term>; therefore you rely on greed <term>Geitz; a grasping, selfish avarice</term> and want only to devour the fat of the earth. You take what you have by force and not by right. The "right" that you claim has been invented by your false, greedy heart; you live only in deception. You persuade and deceive yourself to your own detriment. If you were wise <note>original: *witzig*; in this period, it meant having spiritual discernment or good sense rather than being humorous</note>, you would look toward your end and what follows after this. But you blind yourself with haughtiness <term>Hoffart; external pride or worldly vanity</term> and yet say: "Behold, the golden time!" Many would have wished to see what we see and hear what we hear, yet they have not seen nor heard it.

Yes, listen, for it will also be a testimony against you and make your judgment all the more severe. Up until now, you have not become better, but worse. Therefore know what has been proclaimed to you: that was your own prophet, who called you back from your pride into the mother of humility <note>The "mother of humility" refers to the essential spiritual state of submission to God from which true life grows</note. But you have only become worse and have broken the Spirit’s sword <note>A reference to the "sword of the Spirit," the Word of God, as mentioned in Ephesians 6:17</note>, so that you may do as you please. 

But the Spirit has left you and handed you over to the Turba <term>Turba; in Böhme’s theology, the "disturber," a state of chaotic wrath and destruction that awakens when the divine order is rejected</term>, which shall devour you, just as happened to Israel in ancient times. No counsel helps; your alliances are all void because you rely on the arm of the flesh <note>A biblical reference to Jeremiah 17:5, warning against trusting in human power instead of God</note>. Thus **GOTT** <note>original: *GOTT*; German for God, capitalized and bolded in the original for emphasis</note> has also departed from you and lets you carry on, so that you devour yourself. He teaches when the Lord commands it within him, whether to friends or enemies, at a time convenient for people or inconvenient <note>This echoes the biblical exhortation to be prepared "in season and out of season" (2 Timothy 4:2)</note>. He considers that God does it in him as He wishes, and if he must suffer <term>disgrace: original "Schmach," referring to social shame or public insult</term> for it, it is all the same to him. If someone tips their hat to him <note>In the 17th century, removing one's hat was a mandatory sign of social deference to superiors; the author suggests the true Christian is unmoved by such earthly honors</note>, he humbles himself before God and his brothers, giving the honor to God and his brothers and taking none of it for himself. 

But if someone then curses him and strikes him in the face, he thinks: "I am following Christ, and I stand now in His state of persecution; it shall serve for the best for me and my brother." See, dear brothers, that is a Christian! And God offers such a thing to you now through the wondrous <term>trumpet-blast: original "Posaunenschall," a reference to the apocalyptic heralds in the Book of Revelation</term> of His Spirit. Such a kingdom shall and must soon be revealed and come into being as a testimony over all the peoples of the earth, of which all the prophets have prophesied. 

On the other hand, He offers to all godless, unwilling people His wrath, fury, and <term>hardening: original "Verstockung," the spiritual state of being closed off to divine grace</term>, to consume them and to make an end of <term>Babel: a common mystical and Pietist term for the corrupt, worldly church and social systems</term>. This is said not by me, but by the Spirit of Wonders of all

Thus end the one hundred and fifty prophecies and revelations which the highly enlightened Böhme—moved by his <term>Wonder-spirit</term> <note>original: "Wundergeist"; in Böhme's thought, this refers to the miraculous, creative spirit of God that bypasses human reason to reveal divine truths.</note>—left behind as the strongest witness of the **Jesus-monarchy**. O **Germany, Germany!** Take note of what your crown-prophet Böhme has prophesied! Consider well what is revealed to you here! Your temporal and eternal salvation is at stake, though you may rebel against it as you please!

# A Thorough and True
## Description of the Threefold
### Life in Man.

->Namely:<-

1. Of the life of the spirit of this world in the quality and government of the stars and elements.
2. Of the life of the origin <note>original: "Urkundes"; in Böhme’s vocabulary, this refers to the primal source, record, or manifestation from which all existence springs.</note> of all beings / which stands in the eternal bond / wherein the root of the human soul resides.
3. Of the Paradisiacal life in the <term>Holy Ternary</term> <note>original: "Ternario Sancto"; a Latin term used by Böhme to describe the divine, three-layered spiritual realm or the "body" of the Trinity where God’s glory is manifested.</note> : Namely of the life in the new rebirth / which is the life of the Lord Jesus Christ : Wherein the angelic <note>original: "Englische"; in 17th-century German, this word often meant "angelic" (from "Engel") rather than "English."</note> life is understood / as well as the holy life of the newly reborn human.

Everything thoroughly explored in the light of eternal nature for the comfort of poor, sick, and wounded souls / to seek the holy life in the new rebirth / in which they depart from the earthly life / and enter into the life of Jesus Christ the Son of God.

### Dialogue / of a hungry / thirsty soul ###

[...to say], as she heard that she had the serpent-image <term>Schlangen-Bild: Jakob Böhme’s term for the corrupted human nature inherited after the Fall, which looks like the serpent that tempted Eve</term> within her, which separated her from God; and that the Devil was so near to her in this image, or rather dwelt within it, mixing her will with false thoughts. She heard that he had so much power over her that she was near to damnation, standing captive in the abyss of Hell within the **Wrath of God** <note>original: "Zorn Gottes"; in Böhme's theology, the 'Wrath' is the foundational, fiery nature of God that becomes 'Hell' when separated from His 'Light' or Love</note>. Because of this, she was on the verge of despairing of God’s grace; only the power of her inner conviction <note>original: "Rügung"; refers to a divine stinging or "rebuke" of the conscience that prevents total despair by keeping the soul's focus on its spiritual state</note> held her back from giving up. Thus, she wrestled within herself between **hope** and **doubt**: what hope built up, doubt broke down again. She remained in constant unrest, until finally the world and all its beautiful splendor became loathsome to her. She no longer wished to trouble herself with any worldly joy, yet even through this, she could not find any rest.

After a time, the **Enlightened Soul** returned to her and found her in such distress, and spoke to her:

**Enlightened Soul:** What is it that you are doing? Do you wish to bring about your own end <note>original: "umb deinen Halß helffen"; literally "to help yourself around the neck," a 17th-century idiom for suicide or self-destruction through despair</note> with your distress? Why do you torment yourself in your own power and will? For you are but a worm, and through your own efforts, your misery only grows greater. Indeed, even if you were to dive into the deepest sea, or could fly to where the day rises, or to the morning dawn, or exalt yourself above the stars, you would still—

This **distressed soul** <note>In the German original, the soul (*Seele*) is grammatically feminine, often personified in this era as a female seeker or the "Bride" of Christ.</note> now began to conduct her course under the **suffering of Christ** <note>original: "Leiden Christi." The idea that a believer must spiritually participate in Christ’s passion to reach a state of grace.</note> and entered into **hope** with divine trust; she became more powerful and stronger from day to day, and her evil inclinations died away within her more and more, until she was placed into the great **kingdom of grace**, and the gates of **divine revelation** and the **heavenly kingdom** were opened within her. Thus she came through faith into the true **rest** <term>Ruhe: A technical term in German mysticism referring to "Sabbath-rest," a state of interior stillness where the soul is free from the turmoil of worldly desires.</term> and became once more a **child of God**: to which end may

->GOD the Father, Son,<-
->and Holy Spirit help us all,<-
->Amen.<-
